kkkdma03.dialogue: You get the impression that someone around here has cleaned house - and this is where they threw all the garbage.
kkkdma03.speaker: DM

kkldma03.dialogue: The door before you is sealed with a Glyph you don't recognize. There is a window in the door, but beyond the window is impenetrable darkness.
kkldma03.speaker: DM

kkodma03.dialogue: You sense a watchful presence in this room - for good or ill, you cannot tell.
kkodma03.speaker: DM

kkpdma04.dialogue: The air is dead still, as if no living thing has passed this way for centuries.
kkpdma04.speaker: DM

kkqdma04.dialogue: You find a handful of common gems - worth 400 gold pieces in all.
kkqdma04.speaker: DM

kkrdma03.dialogue: The stairs drop steeply down. You listen carefully, but all is quiet down below.
kkrdma03.speaker: DM

kwadma03.dialogue: The water in the fountain has a sharp smell and a vaguely ominous sheen. Suspended below the surface, you see a necklace of some kind.
kwadma03.speaker: DM

kwadma04.dialogue: Chiseled into the fountain's base are the words, 'Fountain of the Dead.'
kwadma04.speaker: DM

kkvdma03.dialogue: Ceremonies were once held here, and the stones still radiate feelings of sadness and loss.
kkvdma03.speaker: DM

ywadma03.dialogue: A foul smell emanates from fountain before you.  The water appears black and oily.
ywadma03.speaker: DM

kladma03.dialogue: A feeling quickly grows in your mind - one of death and doom, of souls torn from bodies before their time.
kladma03.speaker: DM

klbdma03.dialogue: The aura of dread increases, and falls upon you like a cloud of doom.
klbdma03.speaker: DM

klcdma03.dialogue: He has been carefully laid to rest, and decorated with his possessions. One gold piece has been placed above his head.
klcdma03.speaker: DM

kwbdma03.dialogue: A little brackish water covers the bottom of the well. Dead insects float in it.
kwbdma03.speaker: DM

kwbdma04.dialogue: Chiseled into the well are the words, 'Well of Restoration.'
kwbdma04.speaker: DM

klfdma03.dialogue: The linens are of very fine quality - worth 17 gold pieces.
klfdma03.speaker: DM

klhdma03.dialogue: The fabrics are very well made - worth 25 gold pieces.
klhdma03.speaker: DM

klidma03.dialogue: The well has gone dry, and you can easily spot the old weapons and armor thrown into it over the years. Only a few have any value.
klidma03.speaker: DM

kljdma03.dialogue: Claws killed this orc, and something has gnawed at the soft parts of its face.
kljdma03.speaker: DM

klkdma03.dialogue: Whatever killed this orc also began to feast on it.
klkdma03.speaker: DM

klldma03.dialogue: This orc seems to have been a leader or shaman.
klldma03.speaker: DM

klmdma03.dialogue: It seems this lizard was once a powerful warrior. Someone has carefully composed his body, and placed a single gold piece above his head.
klmdma03.speaker: DM

klndma03.dialogue: You notice a trail of blood leading away under this door.
klndma03.speaker: DM

klodma03.dialogue: This body lies in a pool of blood. A single gold piece has been placed above its head.
klodma03.speaker: DM

kludma03.dialogue: It seems no one has been here in a long time.
kludma03.speaker: DM

klvdma03.dialogue: This place is moist and chill, and smells of the deep earth.
klvdma03.speaker: DM

klwdma03.dialogue: Dark red-brown liquid in the well burbles up slowly, like mud from deep below.
klwdma03.speaker: DM

klxdma03.dialogue: It's no good. The contents dried up long ago, and only dirt remains.
klxdma03.speaker: DM

klydma02.dialogue: There is only hard, dried mud in the bottom of the fountain.
klydma02.speaker: DM

klydma04.dialogue: The liquid tastes like liquid rock and sits heavy in your gut. It makes you heavier and more solid...
klydma04.speaker: DM

klydma05.dialogue: ...but now you move more slowly and exude less charisma.
klydma05.speaker: DM

wbtdma00.dialogue: In the exact center of the sturdy door, there is a small keyhole rimmed in pale blue. Through the keyhole waft the rich odors of the deep earth.
wbtdma00.speaker: DM

wbtdma01.dialogue: The keyhole to this door is rimmed in pale blue.
wbtdma01.speaker: DM

kmkdma03.dialogue: A chill, barely noticeable at first, now begins to creep up from the floor into your bones.
kmkdma03.speaker: DM

kmldma03.dialogue: You notice the floor is no longer unusually cold. All over this chamber, ice is thawing and cracking.
kmldma03.speaker: DM

kvpdma03.dialogue: The cold has collected in this corner, and frozen this door solidly shut.
kvpdma03.speaker: DM

kmmdma03.dialogue: Here too the floor is bitterly cold, with a chill that clutches at your heart.
kmmdma03.speaker: DM

kmndma03.dialogue: This room is colder yet, and numbs the mind.
kmndma03.speaker: DM

kmodma03.dialogue: Cold air pours out the doorway, its touch enveloping you like the caress of death.
kmodma03.speaker: DM

kmpdma03.dialogue: Heavy blows have smashed this well. It is dry and devoid of any chill whatsoever.
kmpdma03.speaker: DM

kmqdma03.dialogue: These wells hold some kind of turgid substance, so cold as to be impossible to drink.
kmqdma03.speaker: DM

kmrdma03.dialogue: You release something made of coldness itself - but before it dies, it flings itself on you.
kmrdma03.speaker: DM

kmsdma03.dialogue: You feel something pass from the room, heading north, back to the ice fields that spawned it.
kmsdma03.speaker: DM

kmsdma04.dialogue: Slowly at first, the room begins to thaw.
kmsdma04.speaker: DM

kmtdma03.dialogue: The orcs are frozen solid, and all their equipment useless and brittle.
kmtdma03.speaker: DM

lmrdma03.dialogue: A frozen blast envelops you as the well crumbles to icy dust.
lmrdma03.speaker: DM

lmsdma03.dialogue: The well explodes -- ice-crystal shards tear at your skin and clothing, and pierce your armor.
lmsdma03.speaker: DM

kmudma03.dialogue: Something big has been moving through this area, and left huge drag marks all over the floor.
kmudma03.speaker: DM

kmydma03.dialogue: You can barely tell that once this was a beautiful hall, richly furnished, filled with light and song.
kmydma03.speaker: DM

knbdma03.dialogue: This chamber was richly furnished once. Visions of lordly folk glimmer briefly in your mind, and then are utterly gone.
knbdma03.speaker: DM

knfdma03.dialogue: The stench flowing from this room is nearly unbearable.
knfdma03.speaker: DM

knhdma03.dialogue: Everything here is dry and dusty.
knhdma03.speaker: DM

knidma03.dialogue: It feels peaceful here, and restful, as if some presence was wordlessly inviting you to pause in your travels.
knidma03.speaker: DM

mnjdma03.dialogue: As you pass under the arches, the room about you goes strangely quiet - not frighteningly so, but softly, comfortably silent.
mnjdma03.speaker: DM

knkdma03.dialogue: The orogs seem to have died peacefully, and lain undisturbed here for some time.
knkdma03.speaker: DM

knldma03.dialogue: The silence here is uneasy, as if watchful beings lurk just out of sight.
knldma03.speaker: DM

knwdma03.dialogue: You can tell someone lives here - but they've been gone for some days.
knwdma03.speaker: DM

knydma03.dialogue: The stones all around it are well-worn, but the fountain itself is dry, empty save for a bit of dust.
knydma03.speaker: DM

knzdma03.dialogue: This looks like it was once a library.
knzdma03.speaker: DM

vbvdma00.dialogue: You stumble upon some old armor, battered and worthless. From the size of it, you guess it was once worn by a derro.
vbvdma00.speaker: DM

jzyDMYA.dialogue: Someone or something has been clawing mindlessly at this door.
jzyDMYA.speaker: DM

jzsDMYA.dialogue: You hear a ghostly giggle, and sense rather than see someone disappear to the northwest. A jasmine scent hangs in the air.
jzsDMYA.speaker: DM

jzcDMYA.dialogue: The ancient waysign is scarred but legible. It indicates the 'Turgild Square' can be found to the south, and the 'Great Hall' lies directly north.
jzcDMYA.speaker: DM

jzcDMYB.dialogue: The waysign indicates 'Turgild Square' to the south, and 'Great Hall' to the north.
jzcDMYB.speaker: DM

jztDMYA.dialogue: You catch the scent of jasmine, and sense a form sashaying away to the northeast, through the wall to the room beyond.
jztDMYA.speaker: DM

jzeDMYA.dialogue: From here, the ruins of a grand thoroughfare disappear into the gloom to the east.
jzeDMYA.speaker: DM

jzxDMYA.dialogue: You see signs that lots of creatures drink at this well.
jzxDMYA.speaker: DM

jzxDMYB.dialogue: You see signs that lots of creatures drink at this well. Your ranger can tell that most of them are skeletons and other undead.
jzxDMYB.speaker: DM

jzxDMYC.dialogue: You see signs that lots of creatures drink at this well. Your rangers can tell that the skeletons and other undead.
jzxDMYC.speaker: DM

jzoDMYA.dialogue: There is a sudden whisper of movement among you - the grumble of dwarves and the clunk of rusty armor. It fades out to the north.
jzoDMYA.speaker: DM

jzfDMYA.dialogue: Ahead of you, in the gloom, is the city square. But the arched hall no longer rings with laughter, and it seems likely the public wells have long since gone dry.
jzfDMYA.speaker: DM

jzaDMYA.dialogue: This ground looks recently disturbed. The marks are hard to read, but you can tell that orcs rested here for a while, then continued on their way north.
jzaDMYA.speaker: DM

jzaDMYB.dialogue: This ground looks recently disturbed. The marks are hard to read, but your ranger can tell that six orcs rested here for a while, then continued on their way north.
jzaDMYB.speaker: DM

jzaDMYC.dialogue: This ground looks recently disturbed. The marks are hard to read, but your rangers agree on this: six orcs rested here for a while, then continued on their way north.
jzaDMYC.speaker: DM

jzvDMYA.dialogue: The prison cell seems to be occupied.
jzvDMYA.speaker: DM

jzgDMYA.dialogue: This great room seems unusually tidy. Even the floor has been swept clean in spots.
jzgDMYA.speaker: DM

jznDMYA.dialogue: Something very heavy just shook the ground to the south!
jznDMYA.speaker: DM

kxwDMYA.dialogue: The ancient waysign indicates that 'Bedlam Prison' can be found to the south, down the stairs.
kxwDMYA.speaker: DM

kxwDMYB.dialogue: It warns visitors 'not to bring keys into the prison, by order of the Warden of the Keys.'
kxwDMYB.speaker: DM

kxwDMYC.dialogue: It's likely the Warden has been dead for centuries, however.
kxwDMYC.speaker: DM

kxwDMYD.dialogue: The waysign indicates 'Bedlam Prison' to the south, and warns visitors not to bring keys into the prison.
kxwDMYD.speaker: DM

jziDMYA.dialogue: Suddenly you feel dwarf ghosts among you, clanking in their rusty armor. A lock thuds shut. Then they are gone.
jziDMYA.speaker: DM

jziDMYB.dialogue: Again you hear the grumble of dwarves and the clunk of rusty armor. A lock thuds shut. Then - nothing.
jziDMYB.speaker: DM

jziDMYC.dialogue: Suddenly you hear dwarves among you - their rusty armor faintly clanking. They murmur approval, and then are heard no more.
jziDMYC.speaker: DM

jzhDMYA.dialogue: You enter the dwarven tombs. Dust lies heavy in this once-great hall, but you sense its dead sleep uneasily, if they sleep at all.
jzhDMYA.speaker: DM

jzhDMYB.dialogue: You step again into the dwarven Hall of the Dead.
jzhDMYB.speaker: DM

kvsDMYA.dialogue: The floor here seems to have been swept clean.
kvsDMYA.speaker: DM

kvsDMYB.dialogue: Your ranger can tell that someone has carefully swept away all the footprints in this area.
kvsDMYB.speaker: DM

kvsDMYC.dialogue: Your rangers can tell that someone has carefully swept away all the footprints in this area.
kvsDMYC.speaker: DM

kucDMYA.dialogue: You sense that a powerful creature recently held court here - maybe an alhoon.
kucDMYA.speaker: DM

kucDMYB.dialogue: But it is gone now and its lair plundered.
kucDMYB.speaker: DM

jzlDMYA.dialogue: A ghostly presence glowers in the doorway. It raises a cautionary hand...
jzlDMYA.speaker: DM

jzlDMYB.dialogue: ...then the door slams shut, and it is gone.
jzlDMYB.speaker: DM

jzlDMYC.dialogue: A ghostly presence glowers in the doorway. It raises a cautionary hand...
jzlDMYC.speaker: DM

jzlDMYD.dialogue: ...then the door slams shut, and it is gone.
jzlDMYD.speaker: DM

jzlDMYE.dialogue: Again a ghostly presence fills the doorway. It cautions you not to enter....
jzlDMYE.speaker: DM

jzlDMYF.dialogue: ...then the door slams shut, and it is gone.
jzlDMYF.speaker: DM

jzlDMYG.dialogue: A ghostly form is hovering here. It bows to you, then disappears.
jzlDMYG.speaker: DM

jzjDMYA.dialogue: A faint track here leads out the door to the northwest.
jzjDMYA.speaker: DM

jzjDMYB.dialogue: Your ranger notices a faint track here. A humanoid carrying something heavy stayed here for a while, then left through the door to the northwest.
jzjDMYB.speaker: DM

jzjDMYC.dialogue: One of your rangers notices a faint track here. A humanoid carrying something heavy stayed here for a while, then left through the door to the northwest.
jzjDMYC.speaker: DM

jzpDMYA.dialogue: You hear the crunch of dainty footsteps, which pass right among you heading to the northeast. A brush of gossamer, a whiff of jasmine, then - nothing.
jzpDMYA.speaker: DM

jzrDMYA.dialogue: In a gossamer flurry a ghost flits off far to the west, leaving only a trace of jasmine in the air.
jzrDMYA.speaker: DM

jzrDMYB.dialogue: Someone giggles softly with anticipation - but there is nothing here but the faint scent of jasmine.
jzrDMYB.speaker: DM

jzbDMYA.dialogue: Some creature has marked this doorjamb with a particularly nasty scent.
jzbDMYA.speaker: DM

kvrDMYA.dialogue: You see ruined walls and gaping doorways. Generations of creatures have plundered this area for stone and wood to fortify their lairs.
kvrDMYA.speaker: DM

kvtDMYA.dialogue: You arrive at a crossroads. Over the years, untold thousands of creatures have died trying to win control of this strategic spot. Of their struggle, nothing remains but bits of bone.
kvtDMYA.speaker: DM

kvuDMYA.dialogue: According to the signpost, you've just come from the Avenue of Smiths.
kvuDMYA.speaker: DM

kvuDMYB.dialogue: To the north is the Grand Avenue; to the south, Apothecary Row. The Stone Flower Halls lie to the west.
kvuDMYB.speaker: DM

kvuDMYC.dialogue: According to the signpost, you've just come from the Stone Flower Halls.
kvuDMYC.speaker: DM

kvuDMYD.dialogue: To the north is the Grand Avenue; to the south, Apothecary Row. The Avenue of Smiths lies to the east.
kvuDMYD.speaker: DM

kvuDMYE.dialogue: According to the signpost, you've just come from the Grand Avenue.
kvuDMYE.speaker: DM

kvuDMYF.dialogue: To the west are the Stone Flower Halls; to the south, Apothecary Row. The Avenue of Smiths lies to the east.
kvuDMYF.speaker: DM

kvuDMYG.dialogue: According to the signpost, you've just come from Apothecary Row.
kvuDMYG.speaker: DM

kvuDMYH.dialogue: To the west are the Stone Flower Halls; to the north, the Grand Avenue. The Avenue of Smiths lies to the east.
kvuDMYH.speaker: DM

kvuDMYI.dialogue: The signpost indicates the Grand Avenue is to the north; Apothecary Row is to the south; the Avenue of Smiths is to the east, and Stone Flower Halls lie to the west.
kvuDMYI.speaker: DM

kvuDMYJ.dialogue: Of these once-happy places, almost nothing remains.
kvuDMYJ.speaker: DM

kvxDMYA.dialogue: You sense a landmark of some kind looming up ahead.
kvxDMYA.speaker: DM

kvvDMYA.dialogue: You sense a landmark of some kind looming up ahead.
kvvDMYA.speaker: DM

kvwDMYA.dialogue: You sense a landmark of some kind looming up ahead.
kvwDMYA.speaker: DM

kvyDMYA.dialogue: You sense a landmark of some kind looming up ahead.
kvyDMYA.speaker: DM

xudDMYA.dialogue: These halls have been torn down and rebuilt many times - most recently, by someone with little skill.
xudDMYA.speaker: DM

vakdma00.dialogue: The orc chief, Zud, has a crude iron key in his clenched fist. It is a small key, such as those used for treasure chests.
vakdma00.speaker: DM

vabdma00.dialogue: Looking into the chest, your eye is immediately drawn to an ornate staff.
vabdma00.speaker: DM

vabdma01.dialogue: Looking closely, you see the staff is laced with intricate runes, writ in a fine elvish hand, and more plainly, the name 'Deathbane.'
vabdma01.speaker: DM

vbtdma00.dialogue: Although the chest holds a fine warhammer, a potion, and some gold, you find your eye drawn first to one small, pale blue key at the bottom.
vbtdma00.speaker: DM

vajdma00.dialogue: Tumbled with the remains of a human woman, you find a pair of enchanted boots, made of snakeskin.
vajdma00.speaker: DM

vajdma01.dialogue: Branded on one of them is the name 'Ozama.'
vajdma01.speaker: DM

vaidma00.dialogue: When the naga dies, the darkness in his lair lifts.
vaidma00.speaker: DM

vaidma01.dialogue: On the naga's body you find a rare necklace indeed - the Wizard's Torc, a great sweeping arc of gold, finely inscribed with arcane symbols.
vaidma01.speaker: DM

vaidma02.dialogue: As you lift it up, you notice that something is missing from its center.
vaidma02.speaker: DM

vaidma03.dialogue: Suddenly the Starstone you bear leaps from its pouch, and shoots through the air over to the Wizard's Torc!
vaidma03.speaker: DM

vaidma04.dialogue: You have restored the Starstone to the Wizard's Torc. The Torc will now open the Circle of Ualair the Silent, just as Harldain told you.
vaidma04.speaker: DM

vaidma05.dialogue: Harldain told you the Torc was missing its Starstone. To restore the power of the Wizard's Torc, you must reunite it with the Starstone he gave you - which is now probably in the greedy hands of Nottle the Scavenger.
vaidma05.speaker: DM

vbbdma00.dialogue: In the ormyrr's pouch you discover his 'magic twig' - a magic wand, its power all but gone.
vbbdma00.speaker: DM

wbbdma00.dialogue: As he died, the orc captain Mol dropped his lead mace - it clattered to the floor cracking some of the stones it landed on.
wbbdma00.speaker: DM

vahdma00.dialogue: In the coffin you find a necklace of breathtaking beauty - and it glows with the blessing of Haela Brightaxe, the dwarven goddess of battle.
vahdma00.speaker: DM

vahdma01.dialogue: It was the prized possession of the dwarf lord Onglore, who prided himself on being first into battle.
vahdma01.speaker: DM

kiczic02.dialogue: 'Higbin: The ceremony ended too soon. The man's name is Faldis. Wait a fortnight, then take what he no longer needs. And do not fail to give me my share. -K'
kiczic02.speaker: Tscroll

tabgas02.dialogue: You are worthy. I will help you bring rest to the Lifespring Guardian.  Look for me... at the Fountain of Stone...
tabgas02.speaker: Garras
tabgas02.desc: null: LOCALIZERS: This text line combines 1.0 and 1.1: First line spoken, ethereally, with ghost effect; second line spoken, ethereally, fading out with ghost effect

tabgas04.dialogue: Many thanks, strangers, for this small kindness.
tabgas04.speaker: Garras
tabgas04.desc: null: LOCALIZERS: spoken, ethereally, with ghost effect, fading away

tacele02.dialogue: You have made a friend. I will help you bring rest to the Lifespring Guardian.  We will meet again... at the Fountain of Stone...
tacele02.speaker: Elena
tacele02.desc: null: LOCALIZERS: This text line combines 1.0 and 1.1: First line spoken, ethereally, with ghost effect; second line spoken, ethereally, fading out with ghost effect

tacele04.dialogue: You have given me peace... and I thank you.
tacele04.speaker: Elena
tacele04.desc: null: LOCALIZERS: spoken, ethereally, with ghost effect, fading away

kitdma00.dialogue: As you approach, many-legged small things scurry back into the barrel.
kitdma00.speaker: DM

kixzix02.dialogue: The inscription reads, 'Juliban Genshihir, Wizard of Air, is at rest here. He was the last Keeper of Shaundakul's Gift, the Earthborn Wind.'
kixzix02.speaker: Jcoffin

kjadmaYA.dialogue: Blessing winds begin to flow from deep underground, up into the three Channel openings overhead.
kjadmaYA.speaker: DM

taddmaYA.dialogue: You hear healing energy flow again, up into the wells of Turgild Square.
taddmaYA.speaker: DM

taedmaYA.dialogue: As Elena's ghost fades away, you hear healing energy flow again from the Lifespring, up into the wells of Turgild Square.
taedmaYA.speaker: DM

tafdmaYA.dialogue: As Garras' ghost fades away, you hear healing energy flow again from the Lifespring, up into the wells of Turgild Square.
tafdmaYA.speaker: DM

tagdmaYA.dialogue: Reunited at last, the two ghosts fade away, and you hear healing energy flow again from the Lifespring, up into the wells of Turgild Square.
tagdmaYA.speaker: DM

khwdma03.dialogue: It seems this sturdy door can only be unlocked from the other side.
khwdma03.speaker: DM

khxdma03.dialogue: The foul air here has a familiar chill. You have returned to the deepest part of the dungeons.
khxdma03.speaker: DM

khyDM00.dialogue: Shashakiro, the Splashing Word, unseals the Glyph of Water.
khyDM00.speaker: DM

khydma04.dialogue: This Glyph seems to have something to do with water.
khydma04.speaker: DM

khzDM00.dialogue: Shashakiro, the Splashing Word, unseals the Glyph of Water.
khzDM00.speaker: DM

khzdma04.dialogue: A Glyph seals this door. You think maybe it is the Glyph of Water.
khzdma04.speaker: DM

kiadma03.dialogue: The Rune on the floor is the famous sigil of the god Clangeddin Silverbeard, the dwarven Father of Battle.
kiadma03.speaker: DM

kiadma04.dialogue: Someone has flanked it with crude arrangements of sharpened sticks.
kiadma04.speaker: DM

kihdma03.dialogue: The inscription reads, 'Faldis - Who Never Fell In Battle.'
kihdma03.speaker: DM

kiidma03.dialogue: Above the door is carved a gem in a mountain - the famous sigil of the dwarf god Dumathoin, The Keeper of Secrets.
kiidma03.speaker: DM

kiidma05.dialogue: The sign of Dumathoin is carved overhead.
kiidma05.speaker: DM

kijdma03.dialogue: The sign of Dumathoin is carved overhead.
kijdma03.speaker: DM

kildma00.dialogue: This is the diary of Faldis, a warrior of old Myth Drannor.
kildma00.speaker: DM

kilzil03.dialogue: 'Here in my last days, all honor me for my courage. I bury my secret here with me: courage had I none! What I had was... '
kilzil03.speaker: fdiary

kilzil04.dialogue: '...a stout shield, and the wit to have it enchanted.  May any who find it show more courage than I did.'
kilzil04.speaker: fdiary

kizdmaYA.dialogue: It seems an elf named Garras was hurriedly buried here.
kizdmaYA.speaker: DM

kizdma04.dialogue: The remains inside his coffin have been moved around a bit.
kizdma04.speaker: DM

kizdma06.dialogue: The remains inside this coffin have been thoroughly disturbed.
kizdma06.speaker: DM

kizdma10.dialogue: From the remains, you discern that Garras was an elf hero of house Maerdrym. He still clutches a scarf embroidered with the name 'Elena,' of House Turgild.
kizdma10.speaker: DM

kizdmaYB.dialogue: He was buried in a hurry, probably in the last days before Myth Drannor's fall. Since then, someone has opened up the coffin and shifted some of his bones.
kizdmaYB.speaker: DM

kizdma12.dialogue: The bones are now in complete disarray. You can't tell who or what was buried here.
kizdma12.speaker: DM

kizdma15.dialogue: You can't make sense out of the jumble of bones.
kizdma15.speaker: DM

kizdma17.dialogue: You carefully bring the skeleton back into a restful and dignified pose.
kizdma17.speaker: DM

kizdma18.dialogue: You pull up everything and look everywhere, but find nothing of value.
kizdma18.speaker: dm

kizpro01.dialogue: Compose the remains as best you can
kizpro01.speaker: Protagonist

kizpro02.dialogue: Search the coffin thoroughly for treasure
kizpro02.speaker: Protagonist

kiodmaYA.dialogue: You see an elf named Elena was put to rest here.
kiodmaYA.speaker: DM

kiodma04.dialogue: Someone has had some rude fun with her bones, putting feet where the hands should be.
kiodma04.speaker: DM

kiodma06.dialogue: The remains inside this coffin have been thoroughly disturbed.
kiodma06.speaker: DM

kiodma10.dialogue: From what little is left of the headstone, you discern that Elena, a high elf of House Turgild, is buried here. She chose to stay in the City, and died just  before its fall.
kiodma10.speaker: DM

kiodmaYB.dialogue: Since then, someone has opened up the coffin and shifted some of her bones around.
kiodmaYB.speaker: DM

kiodma12.dialogue: The bones are now in complete disarray. You can't tell who or what was buried here.
kiodma12.speaker: DM

kiodma15.dialogue: You can't make sense out of the jumble of bones.
kiodma15.speaker: DM

kiodma17.dialogue: You carefully bring the skeleton back into a restful and dignified pose.
kiodma17.speaker: DM

kiodma18.dialogue: You pull up everything and look everywhere, but find nothing of value.
kiodma18.speaker: dm

kiopro01.dialogue: Put the bones back in proper order
kiopro01.speaker: Protagonist

kiopro02.dialogue: Search the coffin thoroughly for treasure
kiopro02.speaker: Protagonist

jhddma00.dialogue: Under the smith's table you find something wrapped in rags. It is still warm to the touch.
jhddma00.speaker: DM

kirdma03.dialogue: The air is heavy with the smell of cooked meat.
kirdma03.speaker: DM

jgydma03.dialogue: There is an inscription on the tomb, 'To Aeseder, brother and planeswalker, at rest but not forgotten.  --Kluusar'.
jgydma03.speaker: DM

jgzdma03.dialogue: This private crypt bears the sorcerer's symbol of the blood moon.
jgzdma03.speaker: DM

kiyziy03.dialogue: Find the Well. Release the Ruby. Restore the Wind.

kxtDM01.speaker: DM

kxtDM02.dialogue: You re-enter the mysterious Rhonglyn room. It is still bitterly cold in here.
kxtDM02.speaker: DM

kxtDM03.dialogue: This room is nearly identical to other Rhonglyn rooms you've seen - and just as frigid inside.
kxtDM03.speaker: DM

kxtDM04.dialogue: This room is nearly identical to one you've seen before. It too is bitterly cold.
kxtDM04.speaker: DM

kwhDMYA.dialogue: The symbol painted on this door is almost too faint to be made out - a masked dwarf with fiery eyes.
kwhDMYA.speaker: DM

kwhDMYB.dialogue: This could only be Gorm Gulthyn, the dwarven god of guardians, watchfulness, and justice.
kwhDMYB.speaker: DM

kwgDMYA.dialogue: The well is dry, but you see signs that someone has rested here fairly recently.
kwgDMYA.speaker: DM

kwgDMYB.dialogue: Your ranger can tell it was a party of humans, and soon finds a note that was wadded up and hidden under a rock.
kwgDMYB.speaker: DM

kwgDMYC.dialogue: After a lengthy investigation, the rangers in your party uncover a note that was wadded up and hidden under a rock.
kwgDMYC.speaker: DM

kwgDMYD.dialogue: Your rogue finds a note that was wadded up and hidden under a rock.
kwgDMYD.speaker: DM

kwgDMYE.dialogue: One of your rogues finds a note that was wadded up and hidden under a rock.
kwgDMYE.speaker: DM

kwgDMYF.dialogue: 'Thumtal, Emmeric: we killed the creatures laired here - a dark naga and many minions - so the rooms around here should be safe for a while. No sign yet of the Room we seek. We will go up the stair far north of here - follow us as soon as you can. -Athan
kwgDMYF.speaker: DM

kweDMYA.dialogue: Charred scraps litter the area around the furnace. It seems many books have been burned here.

kweDMYB.dialogue: The flame in the furnace gleams a little brighter in anticipation.
kweDMYB.speaker: DM

kxxDMYA.dialogue: Far off you hear keys jingling.
kxxDMYA.speaker: DM

kzbDMYA.dialogue: The writing here has been worn smooth with the passing centuries.

kzbDMYC.dialogue: The writing here has been worn smooth with the passing centuries...
kzbDMYC.speaker: DM

kzbDMYD.dialogue: ...but your sharp-eyed ranger manages to read the inscription nevertheless.
kzbDMYD.speaker: DM

kzbDMYE.dialogue: The writing here has been worn smooth with the passing centuries...
kzbDMYE.speaker: DM

kzbDMYF.dialogue: ...but working together your sharp-eyed rangers manage to read the inscription nevertheless.

kzbDMYG.dialogue: The writing here has been worn smooth with the passing centuries...

kzbDMYH.dialogue: ...but by running a trained hand over the stone, your rogue manages to coax the message forth by touch.

kzbDMYI.dialogue: The writing here has been worn smooth with the passing centuries...
kzbDMYI.speaker: DM

kzbDMYJ.dialogue: ...but by running their trained hands over the stone, your rogues manage to coax the message forth by touch.
kzbDMYJ.speaker: DM

kzbDMYK.dialogue: The inscription reads, 'THIS IS THE WELL OF THE EARTHBORN WIND, a Gift given unto the Dwarvenfolk of Myth Drannor by Shaundakul, the Windrider, the God of the Helping Hand.
kzbDMYK.speaker: DM

kzbDMYL.dialogue: 'May the Blessing Breezes it brings up from the untrammeled Depths ever refresh the Peaceful Peoples of the City of Song.'

vaqdma00.dialogue: When the ice shatters, you free the Rhonglyn! You feel the ancient magical devices coming back to life throughout the Dungeons.

vaqdma01.dialogue: Under the ice you find a strange item: a knife sculpted from a sliver of blue ice, chill and electric to the touch.
vaqdma01.speaker: DM

vardma01.dialogue: You find a heavy club, with words spun of silver embedded in its haft...
vardma01.speaker: DM

vardma02.dialogue: 'Root split stone, leaf drink mist, twig grow into Mountain Fist.'
vardma02.speaker: DM

jwtdmaYA.dialogue: It looks like this prison guard starved to death at his post.
jwtdmaYA.speaker: DM

jwudmaYA.dialogue: When the spectre is destroyed, his prized key ring becomes corporeal again, and falls to the ground.
jwudmaYA.speaker: DM

jwudmaYB.dialogue: But the keys have all been worn smooth by centuries of mindless locking and unlocking of doors. You throw the useless thing away.

kzgDM00.dialogue: This wall once had painting on it. You see faint outlines of what might have been a ceremonial scene...

kzgDM01.dialogue: ...maybe set in Turgild Square, up in the Main Halls. Try as you might, no one in your party can make out the details.
kzgDM01.speaker: DM

kzgDM02.dialogue: ...with some effort, your ranger traces out the details.
kzgDM02.speaker: DM

kzgDM03.dialogue: ...with some effort, your rangers trace out the details.
kzgDM03.speaker: DM

kzgDM04.dialogue: ...your rogue soon skillfully traces out the details.

kzgDM05.dialogue: ...your rogues soon skillfully trace out the details.

Ea1mou00.dialogue: Stand away! Heed my warning! Do not touch this sword, unless you are willing to take my place in the Tomb of Eternal Sleep. I, Eadred son of Endoros, have spoken.
Ea1mou00.speaker: Mouth
Ea1mou00.desc: spoken, stern, in Eadred's voice, but enhanced and magical

Ea1dm00.dialogue: The voice seems to emanate from the sword itself!
Ea1dm00.speaker: DM

Ea1ead03.dialogue: So - at last someone dares to wake me. Your need must be very great!
Ea1ead03.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead05.dialogue: Those twisted madmen are here? Then what I dreamed is true - all true. Myth Drannor did fall! I thought - I hoped - it was just an evil dream.
Ea1ead05.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead06.dialogue: Speak no more of evil - but let us avenge it!
Ea1ead06.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead07.dialogue: Who am I? My name you know. I am a man of arms, as my father before me - trained with the sword, the shield, the mace, and the bow.
Ea1ead07.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead08.dialogue: Cleverness - I have none. But no man sees his duty more clearly.
Ea1ead08.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead09.dialogue: As to how I came here - do men still speak of Arms-Captain Hachaam Selorn? And his elf-sword Faervian? Now there was a bladesinger!
Ea1ead09.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead10.dialogue: It was he who slew the lothwight Forgrond, and unwisely tried to claim that foul one's weapon for his own. That is how this cold Tomb claimed him.
Ea1ead10.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead11.dialogue: But - the City needed him - the Weeping War was going badly - do you understand? So I came here and took the sword for my own, and released him. It was my clear duty.
Ea1ead11.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead12.dialogue: And then - what? Selorn must have died, for he never returned to release me. But now you are here in his place, and once again I take up arms to defend the glory of Myth Drannor.
Ea1ead12.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead14.dialogue: Why, I believe one of your company touched the cursed sword. Thus the Tomb released me, but claimed your companion.
Ea1ead14.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead17.dialogue: But you need not fear! Any time you wish - I will be honored to take the sword again, and free the brave soul that took my place in the cold Tomb.
Ea1ead17.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead19.dialogue: Certainly! Do you think I lack courage? It has only grown stronger over the years.
Ea1ead19.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead20.dialogue: Any time you wish - I will be honored to take the sword again, and free the brave soul that took my place in the cold Tomb. Just bid me take up the blade.
Ea1ead20.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead21.dialogue: As I told you - bid me take up the cold blade, and your companion will be freed.
Ea1ead21.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead24.dialogue: Even if my destiny is to die and be forgotten...
Ea1ead24.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead25.dialogue: Until you bid me to grasp again the cold blade of forgetfulness...
Ea1ead25.speaker: Eadred

Ea1ead26.dialogue: For as long as you will have me - I, Eadred son of Endoros, am one of you!
Ea1ead26.speaker: Eadred

Ea1pro01.dialogue: Tell him you are fighting the Cult of the Dragon
Ea1pro01.speaker: Protagonist

Ea1pro02.dialogue: Ask who he is and how he came here
Ea1pro02.speaker: Protagonist

Ea1pro03.dialogue: Ask if he is willing to return to the crypt
Ea1pro03.speaker: Protagonist

Ea1pro04.dialogue: Ask him to come with you
Ea1pro04.speaker: Protagonist

ea3ead01.dialogue: You wish me to grasp the sword? I will.
ea3ead01.speaker: Eadred

ea3ead02.dialogue: But, by your leave, I pause just a moment...
ea3ead02.speaker: Eadred

ea3ead03.dialogue: ...to savor the light, and air, and the warmth of the living.
ea3ead03.speaker: Eadred

ea3ead04.dialogue: There. That is sufficient. Now I return to the cold Tomb...
ea3ead04.speaker: Eadred

ea3ead05.dialogue: Farewell - nay! Say rather, until we meet again.
ea3ead05.speaker: Eadred

ea4ead03.dialogue: Ah, the chill, it has not yet even reached my heart.
ea4ead03.speaker: Eadred
ea4ead03.desc: spoken, booming, shaking off the chill of death

ea4ead04.dialogue: Come, is there more evil? Let us be quick to end it!
ea4ead04.speaker: Eadred

ea4ead05.dialogue: Ah, I am here, I am ready! You call me forth from deep dreams...
ea4ead05.speaker: Eadred
ea4ead05.desc: spoken, a bit disoriented, loudly, as though suddenly up from deep sleep

ea4ead06.dialogue: But I see it was no dream! You have destroyed the Pool, I see it in your faces! Against the greatest odds, you have done what you were sent to do.
ea4ead06.speaker: Eadred

ea4ead07.dialogue: By the Standing Stone, I am honored to travel with you. Is there more evil to smite? Aha! Let us be off!
ea4ead07.speaker: Eadred

ea4ead08.dialogue: By the Standing Stone! There is something about the city now... it has a flicker of the greatness of the old days.
ea4ead08.speaker: Eadred

ea4ead09.dialogue: Now I can say, the centuries in the tomb were not in vain. No, by the Hand of Helm, I am glad the Tomb preserved me, so that I could live to see this day.
ea4ead09.speaker: Eadred

ea4ead10.dialogue: What news? Have you found new evil? Say the word, and I, Eadred son of Endoros, will raise swords with you once more!
ea4ead10.speaker: Eadred

ea4ead11.dialogue: By Helm's Hand! Beriand told us you had succeeded in your quest. And a good thing too!
ea4ead11.speaker: Eadred

ea4ead12.dialogue: For the Cult had come here in force, and hard pressed was I to keep Nottle's head upon his shoulders.
ea4ead12.speaker: Eadred

ea4ead13.dialogue: But then we heard Kya Mordrayn scream! I tell you, everyone on Faerun heard it! And the Cult slogs scattered like leaves on the wind.
ea4ead13.speaker: Eadred

ktkdma03.dialogue: You stand at the base of Castle Cormanthor - the ancient elven fortress of Myth Drannor, and now held by the enemy against you.
ktkdma03.speaker: DM

xuhDM00.dialogue: Once upon a time, this gate was guarded by the elite of the Army of Art, the Akh'Faer, and bladesingers and arms-officers of the Akh'Velahr passed this way to review the defenses of Castle Cormanthor.
xuhDM00.speaker: DM

xuhDM01.dialogue: Today the Captain's Gate stands open, swinging in the cold breeze.
xuhDM01.speaker: DM

kewzew02.dialogue: We have captured one of the traitor orog. Watch out for others.
kewzew02.speaker: trscroll

kfezfe02.dialogue: 'Find out where the rogue orogs are hiding. This prisoner should tell you. Then destroy them all.  -Overseer Scaggik'
kfezfe02.speaker: Scroll

kfkzfk02.dialogue: 'Here lie our loyal comrades. Disturb their slumber at thy peril.'
kfkzfk02.speaker: Amarker

kflzfl02.dialogue: 'Bannoc, son of Enroc, Cleric of Tyr'
kflzfl02.speaker: Acoffin1

kfpzfp02.dialogue: 'Ariana the Archer, proud woman of Westdale'
kfpzfp02.speaker: Acoffin5

kgwdma00.dialogue: The orogs murmur among themselves, but none of them make any kind of threatening move.
kgwdma00.speaker: DM

kgydma00.dialogue: You hear words spoken in a terrible language. The Stone Mouth you carry translates them for you.
kgydma00.speaker: DM

khadma00.dialogue: You hear words spoken in a terrible language. The Stone Mouth you carry translates them for you.
khadma00.speaker: DM

kezdma03.dialogue: It has the refreshing flavor of old elven wine. It heals your body, but it also dulls your reflexes.
kezdma03.speaker: DM

kfadma03.dialogue: It has the refreshing flavor of old elven wine, and heals your body as it lifts your spirits.
kfadma03.speaker: DM

kfbdma03.dialogue: It seems no one has entered here for many years.
kfbdma03.speaker: DM

kfsdma03.dialogue: The gate looks like it has not been opened in decades - its lock is rusted shut.
kfsdma03.speaker: DM

kftdma03.dialogue: The man is freshly dead - from many crushing blows.
kftdma03.speaker: DM

kfudma03.dialogue: This Cult soldier died from a massive blow to the back of the head.
kfudma03.speaker: DM

kfvdma03.dialogue: No sounds at all echo up from the stairwell. Below, all is quiet and dark.
kfvdma03.speaker: DM

kfxdma03.dialogue: The bucket contains a crude pair of tongs and one very dead fish.
kfxdma03.speaker: DM

kfydma03.dialogue: The well is shallow and populated with plants and many fish. At the bottom, you see a strange object sparkling, but cannot make out what it is.
kfydma03.speaker: DM

kfzdma03.dialogue: The well is shallow and populated with plants and many fish. At the bottom, you see a strange object sparkling, but cannot make out what it is.
kfzdma03.speaker: DM

kfzdma05.dialogue: The well is full of fish. Something sparkles at the bottom.
kfzdma05.speaker: DM

kfzdma07.dialogue: As you reach into the cold water of the well, fish dart to your hand and arm and bite them repeatedly.
kfzdma07.speaker: DM

kfzdma10.dialogue: Then you notice sharp, menacing teeth on the fish.
kfzdma10.speaker: DM

kfzdma13.dialogue: Within moments, a fish bobs belly-up to the surface. It is soon followed by many others.
kfzdma13.speaker: DM

kfzdma14.dialogue: You pull up the sparkling object in the well - a shield!
kfzdma14.speaker: DM

kfzdma17.dialogue: There is nothing in the well but some poisoned fish.
kfzdma17.speaker: DM

kfzpro02.dialogue: Pour the Naga poison in the well
kfzpro02.speaker: Protagonist

kgbdma03.dialogue: Past the barrier, you can see a rare prize - one of the Orrery Planets that Harldain mentioned.
kgbdma03.speaker: DM

kgbdma04.dialogue: You see the Orrery Planet is bound to the pole. Harldain hoped you could release it.
kgbdma04.speaker: DM

kgddma02.dialogue: The plaque reads, 'Enter with ease and nourish thy health, but exit with care if thee nourish thy wealth.' Bolts of lightning frame the words.
kgddma02.speaker: DM

sebdma02.dialogue: The plaque reads, 'Enter with ease and nourish thy health, but exit with care if thee nourish thy wealth.' Bolts of lightning frame the words.
sebdma02.speaker: DM

kgedma03.dialogue: The fountain's water is sweet-smelling and almost impossibly clear.
kgedma03.speaker: DM

kgfdma03.dialogue: This has the feel of a mage's chamber, abandoned now for a century at least.
kgfdma03.speaker: DM

kgjdma03.dialogue: This whole wall has been etched with  tiny crescent moons, one after another, hundreds of them in all.
kgjdma03.speaker: DM

kgkdma03.dialogue: On this wall, the phrase 'I Know Nothing' has been etched dozens of times.
kgkdma03.speaker: DM

kgldma03.dialogue: Only parts of the letter can be read: 'Lover, do not despair. There is a secret door... open and... to the right. Meet us by the fountain. Come as soon as... Yours forever...'
kgldma03.speaker: DM

kgmdma03.dialogue: Crudely etched here are the words, 'O my love I could not find it. I am sorry, sorry, sorry - and love you always.
kgmdma03.speaker: DM

kgpdma03.dialogue: Even after hundreds of years, you sense ancient spells hanging like cobwebs in the air of this room.
kgpdma03.speaker: DM

kgrdma03.dialogue: The Circle of Ualair has opened. You have entered the Catacombs, the legendary deep dwelvings under Castle Cormanthor.
kgrdma03.speaker: DM

kwmDMYA.dialogue: The chest is empty, except for a crumpled-up parchment.
kwmDMYA.speaker: DM

kwmDMYB.dialogue: The parchment reads, 'Tulud: things are being stolen. Double the guard on this chest and affix an additional poison trap. - Wikgul
kwmDMYB.speaker: DM

kwmDMYC.dialogue: Your ranger can tell two humanoids left the chest here - one human-sized, and the other a halfling.
kwmDMYC.speaker: DM

kwmDMYD.dialogue: Your rangers can tell two humanoids left the chest here - one human-sized, and the other a halfling.
kwmDMYD.speaker: DM

kxsDM00.dialogue: Although it happened many years ago, this tragedy is writ plain: elven knights made their last stand here against the frenzied yugoloths and nycaloths of the Army of Darkness.
kxsDM00.speaker: DM

kxsDM01.dialogue: Many ghosts crowd around you. One steps forward as their spokesman; her words ring in your mind.
kxsDM01.speaker: DM

kxsDM02.dialogue: 'Long we fought, and well, to hold the stairs against the countless enemy...'
kxsDM02.speaker: DM

kxsDM03.dialogue: 'But through some foul treachery the beasts came up the stairs from behind, and so we were undone.'
kxsDM03.speaker: DM

kxsDM04.dialogue: 'We did not seek glory in life, nor do we in death - but only someone akin to us, to whom we could tell our story.'
kxsDM04.speaker: DM

kxsDM05.dialogue: 'Now we will rest, and trouble you no more.'
kxsDM05.speaker: DM

kxsDM06.dialogue: 'And this also we can tell you - the dark elves have seized the temple to the south. They are strong and treacherous! Seek out every advantage you can, before you take them on and send them out wailing into the light.'
kxsDM06.speaker: DM

kxqDM00.dialogue: You smell wood smoke and the unmistakable stench of burning flesh.
kxqDM00.speaker: DM

kxrDM00.dialogue: The bodies still ooze life, and their corpses look plundered. Yet you see no one else around save the watchful stones.
kxrDM00.speaker: DM

xufDMYA.dialogue: You enter a grand hall, pungent with incense and aromatics. In the hushed silence you sense a godlike presence, urging all to commit acts of wanton chaos.
xufDMYA.speaker: DM

xaddma00.dialogue: You notice something still moving. The pet arraccat's food bowl, kicked during the battle, is still rocking from side to side.
xaddma00.speaker: DM

xaddma01.dialogue: The bowl is actually an elf's skull. You pick it up, and recognize it at once: it is the skull of Anorrweyn Evensong!
xaddma01.speaker: DM

kosdma00.dialogue: The doors appear to be ancient, no longer used. But...
kosdma00.speaker: DM

gosdma00.dialogue: The doors appear to be ancient, no longer used. But...
gosdma00.speaker: DM

koadma03.dialogue: You descend to the second level of the Catacombs. The air seems denser here, and sounds die rather than echo in the atmosphere of gloom.
koadma03.speaker: DM

kobdma03.dialogue: There is a map here, of an area of dungeon. It shows rooms to the north held by the Cult, rooms in the middle rife with undead, and rooms to the south held by 'the Freth.'
kobdma03.speaker: DM

kofdma03.dialogue: In the air lingers the haze of spent flame spells and the faint scent of blood.
kofdma03.speaker: DM

kokdma03.dialogue: For just a moment you have a vision - of mages chanting and portals rending the air - then snap! You are back in the here and now.
kokdma03.speaker: DM

kondma03.dialogue: You notice something - bloody tracks emerge from under the north door, and disappear under the door to the south. There is a whiff of ancient decay in the air.
kondma03.speaker: DM

vcedma00.dialogue: You see a gleam at the bottom of the well. It turns out to be a ring made of ebony - obviously enchanted, because it weighs several hundred pounds! It seems heavy with the burden of death.
vcedma00.speaker: DM

vcedma01.dialogue: This ring's craftsmanship is similar to that of the ivory ring you have.
vcedma01.speaker: DM

vcedma02.dialogue: This ring's craftsmanship is similar to that of the ivory ring you found.
vcedma02.speaker: DM

vcedma03.dialogue: You're reminded of a legend you heard once, about a pair of rings shaped from old Staffs of Power - one white, one black.
vcedma03.speaker: DM

vcedma04.dialogue: With some difficulty, you manage to heft the ebony ring out of the Well of Dreams.
vcedma04.speaker: DM

vcfdma00.dialogue: You find an ivory ring, which floats lightly in your hand. It seems to radiate calm and life.
vcfdma00.speaker: DM

vcfdma01.dialogue: This ring's craftsmanship is similar to that of the ebony ring you have.
vcfdma01.speaker: DM

vcfdma02.dialogue: This ring's craftsmanship is similar to that of the ebony ring you found.
vcfdma02.speaker: DM

vcfdma03.dialogue: You're reminded of a legend you heard once, about a pair of rings shaped from old Staffs of Power - one white, one black.
vcfdma03.speaker: DM

kprzpr02.dialogue: Hold! Hold, I say! I know where lies the Mysterious Chainmail of Nezras! Is that of interest to you? Then hold your weapons and swallow your spells!
kprzpr02.speaker: Naga3

kqidma00.dialogue: It sounds like some humans are talking just on the other side of this door.
kqidma00.speaker: DM

kpjdma02.dialogue: The remains in the sarcophagus have been pawed over, and the head is missing.
kpjdma02.speaker: DM

kpmdma03.dialogue: You are immediately struck by the feeling of an enduring presence. These were the chambers of a powerful person, a wizard most likely, and strong traces of his or her spirit persist.
kpmdma03.speaker: DM

kpndma03.dialogue: Thyaast's journal is written in a powerful flowing script - it's over a thousand pages long.
kpndma03.speaker: DM

kpndma05.dialogue: Thyaast, a promising spellsummoner of the revered House of Ammath, began this journal in the Year of Falling Petals - about fifty years before the fall of Myth Drannor.
kpndma05.speaker: DM

kpndma06.dialogue: She rues the mysterious death of Aravae Irythil, the heir of the Coronal, and fills pages with hopes and opinions of who the city's new leader might be.
kpndma06.speaker: DM

kpndma07.dialogue: She seems completely unaware of the dark forces gathering to assail Myth Drannor.
kpndma07.speaker: DM

kpndma09.dialogue: On these pages, the mage Thyaast recounts the many signs of doom appearing in the city. Chief among them: the flight of Sakaala of the Seven Rings, headmistress of the Incanistaeum, school for wizards.
kpndma09.speaker: DM

kpndma10.dialogue: Thyaast vows that she will never flee the city she loves, and embarks on studies to invent greatspells to use against Myth Drannor's many foes.
kpndma10.speaker: DM

kpndma12.dialogue: The end of the journal is filled with fevered scribblings about arcane matters. Thyaast seems to have discovered a new way to bring the fallen back to life.
kpndma12.speaker: DM

kpndma13.dialogue: The mage's last words are, 'I go tonight out to the dangerous battlefields and spark my Bloodflame... it will leap from fallen to fallen and restore fire to bodies gone cold.'
kpndma13.speaker: DM

kpndma14.dialogue: There is nothing more. The rest of the pages are blank.
kpndma14.speaker: DM

kpodma03.dialogue: You are immediately struck by the feeling of an enduring presence. These were the chambers of a powerful person, a wizard most likely, and strong traces of his or her spirit persist.
kpodma03.speaker: DM

kppdma03.dialogue: The page is dotted with bloodstains, and the writing is shaky and wandering.
kppdma03.speaker: DM

kppdma04.dialogue: Thyaast has written, 'The wound is evil and deep, and the physickers shake their heads. But where the healing hand fails, the wizard's mind may triumph!'
kppdma04.speaker: DM

kppdma05.dialogue: There is more here, which you cannot make out - except for the words 'raise more troops' and  'I live'...
kppdma05.speaker: DM

kpsdma03.dialogue: You descend about a hundred stairs. You find the air here is murky and the atmosphere unwholesome and tainted with dread.
kpsdma03.speaker: DM

kpudma03.dialogue: Writ above the door, in the runes of elves, dwarves and humans, are the words 'Last Repose of the Stout Folk of Myth Drannor.'
kpudma03.speaker: DM

kpudma04.dialogue: In smaller letters, a warning: 'Let Any Who Take Without Giving, Beware!'
kpudma04.speaker: DM

kpvzzq02.dialogue: 'Artoth Frayhammer, builder of the Great Hall'
kpvzzq02.speaker: AFinscr

kpwzzp02.dialogue: 'Give To Me What You Would Take'
kpwzzp02.speaker: FtnInsc

kqfzqf02.dialogue: 'Rolga Stumprock, defender of the Great Hall'
kqfzqf02.speaker: RSinscr

kqjzqj02.dialogue: 'Forsgren: one of the arraccat found its way down to the Baelnorn's keep. This cannot be allowed to happen again. Use traprunes if you must, but exterminate them all. -Scander'
kqjzqj02.speaker: ScrollAR

kxmDMYA.dialogue: An uneasy feeling comes over you. Something unseen is at work here.
kxmDMYA.speaker: DM

kxnDMYA.dialogue: You sense that someone or something is judging you, waiting to see what action you may take.
kxnDMYA.speaker: DM

kxoDM00.dialogue: Again you get the feeling that you are being watched.
kxoDM00.speaker: DM

kwcDM00.dialogue: You hear an indistinct voice beyond the wall.
kwcDM00.speaker: DM

kwcDM01.dialogue: You hear the rumbling voice continue. 'They are just outside,' it says.
kwcDM01.speaker: DM

kwcDM02.dialogue: The voice goes on, 'If they find the door, I may lose a body or two.'
kwcDM02.speaker: DM

kwcDM03.dialogue: 'Kill them well,' the voice commands, 'but leave the bodies intact this time!
kwcDM03.speaker: DM

kxpDM00.dialogue: You are stopped by a ghastly and alarming smell - the stench of putrifying flesh mixed with the sickly sweet smell of arraccat eggs.
kxpDM00.speaker: DM

kxzDMYA.dialogue: This would seem to be the place Nathlilik described to you, guarded by a Cult Mage wielding the Staff of Sunlight.
kxzDMYA.speaker: DM

kxzDMYB.dialogue: There is no one here. But your ranger detects signs of recent struggle, and the claw marks of arraccat.
kxzDMYB.speaker: DM

kxzDMYC.dialogue: There is no one here. But one of your rangers detects signs of recent struggle, and another makes out clearly the claw marks of many arraccat.
kxzDMYC.speaker: DM

kxzDMYD.dialogue: But there is no one here, and no sign except some fresh blood smears on the floor.
kxzDMYD.speaker: DM

kxzDMYE.dialogue: This is the place Nathlilik told you about, guarded by the Cult Mage wielding the Staff of Sunlight, deadly to drow.
kxzDMYE.speaker: DM

kxzDMYF.dialogue: You see signs that arraccat attacked the mage, and dragged him back to their lair.
kxzDMYF.speaker: DM

xaedma00.dialogue: Your eye is drawn to a corpse of a Cult Mage, most recently sucked dry and tossed upon the arraccat's bone pile.
xaedma00.speaker: DM

xaedma01.dialogue: The corpse still grips a golden stave. Examining it, you realize it is one of the legendary Sacred Staffs of Sunlight, created by Bedine nomads to honor their sun god, At'ar the Merciless.
xaedma01.speaker: DM

gredma00.dialogue: You hear words spoken in a terrible language. The Stone Mouth you carry translates them for you.
gredma00.speaker: DM

krsdmaYA.dialogue: You draw near to a group of drow. They are intent on an impending duel.
krsdmaYA.speaker: DM

kqqdma03.dialogue: The stairs go climbing steeply up. Whoever has been using them has tracked in a lot of dirt.
kqqdma03.speaker: DM

kqqdma05.dialogue: At the top you find a key left in this door.
kqqdma05.speaker: DM

krgdma03.dialogue: You sense that the drow have cast spells in this space - the walls themselves seem watchful.
krgdma03.speaker: DM

krydma03.dialogue: In the deep of the catacombs, the air is cold and oppressively still. Chaotic fragments of a grim past echo in your mind.
krydma03.speaker: DM

krzdma02.dialogue: 'Valanthe, Clan Amakiir - High Mistress to the Tulun Court'
krzdma02.speaker: dm

ksadma02.dialogue: Eloen, Clan Durothil - He First Sang the Lay Quessircalin'
ksadma02.speaker: dm

kscdma02.dialogue: Kerym, Clan Ildacer - He Forged the Bladesinger Tulut'
kscdma02.speaker: dm

ksddma02.dialogue: Alea, Clan Aunglor - She First Saw the Glimmerstar of Elos'
ksddma02.speaker: dm

ksedma03.dialogue: The inscription here has been hacked away.
ksedma03.speaker: DM

ksfdma03.dialogue: There is nothing inside but rat droppings. You notice the inside of the tomb is marred with deep scars, and over everything hangs an enduring pall of evil.
ksfdma03.speaker: DM

ksgdma02.dialogue: Finolas, Clan Ulondarr - His Arm Laid Low the Fiend Morcan'
ksgdma02.speaker: dm

kshdma02.dialogue: 'Himo, Clan Siannodel - He Slew the Dark Trandel'
kshdma02.speaker: dm

ksidma02.dialogue: It appears someone broke out of, not into, this tomb.
ksidma02.speaker: DM

ksjdma02.dialogue: 'Aolis Ammath, Clan Alastrarra - He Fell in Glory at Erolith's Mound'
ksjdma02.speaker: dm

kskdma02.dialogue: Elidyr, Clan Haladar - He Spoke in Quiet Wisdom'
kskdma02.speaker: dm

ksldma02.dialogue: Penaal Thist, Clan Auglamyr - Beloved Wingrider of Lady Durothil'
ksldma02.speaker: dm

ksmdma02.dialogue: Fieryat, Clan Nierdre - She Led the Shiningstars'
ksmdma02.speaker: dm

ksndma02.dialogue: Laele, Clan Ainesilver - Bestowed the Blessings of Hanali Celanil'
ksndma02.speaker: dm

ksodma03.dialogue: The inscription here has been blotted out, and replaced with a foul rune writ in ever-fresh blood.
ksodma03.speaker: DM

kxkDMYA.dialogue: Far off you hear a vehement argument. One drow loudly invokes the name of 'Greyanna,' but another seems to insist on 'Dreydre.'
kxkDMYA.speaker: DM

kxfDM00.dialogue: You've entered what seems to be the treasure archive of the Freth drow.
kxfDM00.speaker: DM

kxfDM01.dialogue: You faintly hear things being moved beyond the wall to the north.
kxfDM01.speaker: DM

kxgDM00.dialogue: The drow have neatly packed their looted treasures, and the chests stand ready to be transported away - down to the Underdark, probably, and the prizes never again seen by creatures of light.
kxgDM00.speaker: DM

kxhDM00.dialogue: Behold! From the tombs and crannies of the Catacombs, the clever drow have claimed for themselves some of the legendary lost treasures of Myth Drannor.
kxhDM00.speaker: DM

kxhDM01.dialogue: You have opened the place where the drow keep scrolls, parchments and elixirs of magic.
kxhDM01.speaker: DM

kxhDM02.dialogue: A feeling of relief washes over you - as if the items themselves are grateful to be rescued from dark hands.
kxhDM02.speaker: DM

kxhDM03.dialogue: On the chests, you see spidery writing - and the marks of the Noble House of Freth. The First Matron of the House, Ilharess Turushan Freth, is apparently claiming the contents as her personal own.
kxhDM03.speaker: DM

kxiDM00.dialogue: Behold! From the tombs and crannies of the Catacombs, the clever drow have claimed for themselves some of the legendary lost treasures of Myth Drannor.
kxiDM00.speaker: DM

kxiDM01.dialogue: This is the place where the drow store their prized weapons and armor.
kxiDM01.speaker: DM

kxiDM02.dialogue: A feeling of relief washes over you - as if the items themselves are grateful to be rescued from dark hands.
kxiDM02.speaker: DM

kxiDM03.dialogue: On the chests, you see spidery writing - and the marks of the Noble House of Freth. The First Matron of the House, Ilharess Turushan Freth, is apparently claiming the contents as her personal own.
kxiDM03.speaker: DM

kxjDM00.dialogue: Behold! From the tombs and crannies of the Catacombs, the clever drow have claimed for themselves some of the legendary lost treasures of Myth Drannor.
kxjDM00.speaker: DM

kxjDM01.dialogue: Before you are the magic items which the drow deemed most valuable.
kxjDM01.speaker: DM

kxjDM02.dialogue: A feeling of relief washes over you - as if the items themselves are grateful to be rescued from dark hands.
kxjDM02.speaker: DM

em1Emm02.dialogue: Aid comes when least looked for, I see. Well met, friends.
em1Emm02.speaker: Emmeric
em1Emm02.desc: spoken, a little out of breath since they've just finished a battle

em1Emm03.dialogue: If you are from Phlan, as your garb bespeaks, then well met indeed.
em1Emm03.speaker: Emmeric
em1Emm03.desc: Spoken, a little out of breath since they've just finished a battle

em1Emm04.dialogue: Ask rather why I am not slain.
em1Emm04.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm05.dialogue: I'm Emmeric, called 'lucky' in my mother's tongue, though I've come to doubt its prophecy of late.
em1Emm05.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm06.dialogue: These mages and their dark ilk slew all my band, save myself and our leader, Athan.
em1Emm06.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm07.dialogue: They spared the best and the least of us, it seems. For what purpose, I know not.
em1Emm07.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm08.dialogue: Without your aid, the gods know what fate would have befallen me.
em1Emm08.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm09.dialogue: If your cause is just, my blade is at your service.
em1Emm09.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm10.dialogue: In the ruins to the north?  You're mistaken, friends.
em1Emm10.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm11.dialogue: That you found a full count of six burned bodies, I doubt not. But fireballs leave friend and foe looking much alike.
em1Emm11.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm12.dialogue: Athan was beset by winged beasts, vile things under the mages' command. They dragged him into the sky as I woke from the damnable sleep spell.
em1Emm12.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm13.dialogue: I saw him struggle even then, flailing his axe at their wings as they lifted him to the Castle ramparts.
em1Emm13.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm14.dialogue: The great mage Elminster handpicked Athan and his band to venture here. He bid us uncover what evil taints the city's guardian spell, the ancient Mythal.
em1Emm14.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm16.dialogue: Since Myth Drannor's fall, the spell has faded some, but of late, a dark corruption has possessed it and twisted even its last remaining boons to curses.
em1Emm16.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm17.dialogue: Elminster sent us here to discover the cause of the corruption. That we did, but at great cost:  my companions are dead, and the priceless Gauntlets of Moander are stolen by their murderers.
em1Emm17.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm18.dialogue: Some new force has entered Myth Drannor, driven out the laired and lesser evils, and taken possession of Castle Cormanthor.
em1Emm18.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm19.dialogue: The corruption of the Mythal is their doing. They have twisted its power, and used it to raise a Pool of Radiance whose evil might spreads throughout Faerun.
em1Emm19.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm20.dialogue: The Gauntlets hold a singular gift: the power to destroy Pools of Radiance.
em1Emm20.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm21.dialogue: Their palms are graven with eye runes, which have slumbered since the destruction of the Pool at Phlan. A season ago, they snapped open once again, to warn of a new Pool rising.
em1Emm21.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm22.dialogue: Elminster feared that this new Pool could be at the heart of the evil changes newly come over Myth Drannor. He sent us with the Gauntlets to uncover the truth.
em1Emm22.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm23.dialogue: If his fears were founded, and we found such a Pool, we were to use the Gauntlets to destroy it. But rather, we have let them slip into the hands of our enemies.
em1Emm23.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm24.dialogue: My feet may have been bound, but my ears were open: the mages serve a dark mistress who's taken hold of Castle Cormanthor.
em1Emm24.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm25.dialogue: It was to her they took the Gauntlets of Moander, which Elminster himself gave into our keeping.
em1Emm25.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm26.dialogue: I listened for a name to curse, but they spoke of their masters only as 'She' and 'Her'...and sometimes 'Him'....and trembled at the words.
em1Emm26.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm27.dialogue: The mages took from me a ring of great power, sealed onto a skeletal arm.
em1Emm27.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm28.dialogue: They've taken it to the Room of Words, in the hopes of unsealing the ring from its dead wearer's hand.
em1Emm28.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm29.dialogue: Athan believed that that ring, the Ring of Calling, holds the key to attaining the city Heights, where our quest lies.
em1Emm29.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm30.dialogue: Athan believed that the Ring of Calling holds the key to attaining the City Heights, where our quest lies.
em1Emm30.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm31.dialogue: But to wield it, and thereby open the gate at the Circle of Mythanthor, he searched for the Word that will release the ring from its dead master's hand.
em1Emm31.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm32.dialogue: Legend has it that such things can be found in the Hall of Wizards. The portal between these dungeons and the Hall is a ring of colored stones whose magic can bear you from floor to floor.
em1Emm32.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm33.dialogue: He said that only one who wears the ring can open the gate at the Circle of Mythanthor and use it to move freely between the dungeons and the Heights above.
em1Emm33.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm34.dialogue: It was Athan's firm belief that the evil guiding these mages lies at the heart of Castle Cormanthor. He sought to find a way to attack their stronghold there and abolish the threat they pose to Faerun.
em1Emm34.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm36.dialogue: A party of so many would be a danger to itself in this cursed place.
em1Emm36.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm37.dialogue: But if any of your number chose to step aside, I'd gladly take up arms with you. Until then...
em1Emm37.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm38.dialogue: The slain comrades you bear are not yet past saving. But should you see fit to bury them, or if any of your number chooses to step aside from our quest, I'd gladly take up arms with you. Until then...
em1Emm38.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm39.dialogue: Then I will make my way back to Stillwater. The elves there were good friends to us - Faeril led us bleeding out of these dungeons, and Beriand tended our wounds.
em1Emm39.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm40.dialogue: I don't want to bring my bad luck upon them, however, or give away their secret shelter to our enemies. Nottle said he could use someone to guard his wagon...
em1Emm40.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm41.dialogue: My companions are dead and my quest failed, unless it lives with you.
em1Emm41.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm42.dialogue: I admit, I was no match for any in Athan's band when I slipped into their midst. Elminster laughed that I made bold to join them on so dire a journey.
em1Emm42.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm43.dialogue: But my arm has been the end of many a foul creature since then. And my peacock's pride, reborn as watchfulness.
em1Emm43.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm44.dialogue: Let me join with you against this evil, and wet my blade in the blood of those who slew my friends.
em1Emm44.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm45.dialogue: Your numbers are many now, but should any of you choose to step aside from our quest, I'll gladly take up arms with the rest against this evil. Until then...
em1Emm45.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm46.dialogue: Your numbers are many, though some lie between this world and the next. But should you find yourselves few, I'll gladly take up arms with you against this evil. Until then...
em1Emm46.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm47.dialogue: You'll not regret the company of my blade: vengeance makes a fine sharpening stone.
em1Emm47.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm48.dialogue: Then I thank you for my life and for my freedom from this carrion.
em1Emm48.speaker: Emmeric

em1Emm49.dialogue: May whatever gods you hold dear watch your backs. Find me with Nottle, if ever you need another eager blade.
em1Emm49.speaker: Emmeric

em1pro00.dialogue: Ask why he was a prisoner
em1pro00.speaker: Protagonist

em1pro04.dialogue: Ask him if he learned anything from his captors
em1pro04.speaker: Protagonist

em1pro05.dialogue: Tell him you saw Athan's body in the ruins
em1pro05.speaker: Protagonist

em1pro06.dialogue: Ask him where Athan is now
em1pro06.speaker: Protagonist

em1pro08.dialogue: Ask what is corrupting the Mythal
em1pro08.speaker: Protagonist

em1pro09.dialogue: Ask what you can do to further Athan's quest
em1pro09.speaker: Protagonist

em1pro10.dialogue: Ask him about the Gauntlets of Moander
em1pro10.speaker: Protagonist

em1pro11.dialogue: Ask him to join your party
em1pro11.speaker: Protagonist

em1pro12.dialogue: Tell him you must press on
em1pro12.speaker: Protagonist

em2emm02.dialogue: Ah my friends, the city is ringing with tales of your triumph! Did you really kill the dracolich with one blow? And Kya Mordrayn? Did she truly breathe fire? If only I could have been among you!
em2emm02.speaker: Emmeric

em2emm03.dialogue: Ah my friends, the city is ringing with tales of your triumph! Did you really kill the dracolich with one blow? And Kya Mordrayn? Did she truly breathe fire? Say you will have me in your company again!
em2emm03.speaker: Emmeric

em2emm04.dialogue: Ah my companions! Since we slew Pelendralaar, the city rings with tales of your triumphs! Let me join your company again!
em2emm04.speaker: Emmeric

gf1gf102.speaker: gargfly1
gf1gf102.desc: spoken, as a challenge; 'Speak now and answer my summons!'

gf1gf103.speaker: gargfly1
gf1gf103.desc: spoken, as a challenge; 'You will do what the Tusk-Lord says.'

gf1gf104.speaker: gargfly1
gf1gf104.desc: spoken, as a challenge; 'Speak up! The Tusk-Lord has words for you.'

gf1gf105.speaker: gargfly1
gf1gf105.desc: spoken, as a warning; 'You will regret not heeding us.'

gf1gf106.speaker: gargfly1
gf1gf106.desc: spoken, as a challenge; 'Speak up! Speak up! Human-kin, speak now.'

gf1gf107.speaker: gargfly1
gf1gf107.desc: spoken, as a challenge; 'Show me you understand what I'm saying.'

gf1dma00.dialogue: The Stone Mouth you carry translates the gargoyle's words.
gf1dma00.speaker: DM

gf1gf110.dialogue: Speak now, if you are the Great Ones the Tusk-Lord seeks.
gf1gf110.speaker: gargfly1

gf1gf112.dialogue: The Cruel Company! The ones who kill all they meet! The stones of Myth Drannor whisper things about you... the many weaklings you have tortured....
gf1gf112.speaker: gargfly1

gf1gf200.dialogue: The stones drink the blood you spill!
gf1gf200.speaker: Gargfly2

gf1gf113.dialogue: The dark stones sing your bloody song. And so the Tusk-Lord seeks you, if you are the Ones.
gf1gf113.speaker: gargfly1

gf1gf115.dialogue: Are you the Ones? Tell us, and you will come to know who the Tusk-Lord is.
gf1gf115.speaker: gargfly1

gf1gf117.dialogue: Our Tusk-Lord serves no one! And we serve no one but the Tusk-Lord.
gf1gf117.speaker: gargfly1

gf1gf119.dialogue: Are you the Great Ones, or not?
gf1gf119.speaker: gargfly1

gf1gf121.dialogue: The Tusk-Lord seeks weaklings to torture...
gf1gf121.speaker: gargfly1

gf1gf204.dialogue: He doesn't want to meet the Great Ones by mistake!
gf1gf204.speaker: Gargfly2

gf1gf123.dialogue: He wished you to have this token of tribute, here in this box.
gf1gf123.speaker: gargfly1

gf1gf1YB.dialogue: We'll be back, all of us, oik oik oik!
gf1gf1YB.speaker: gargfly1

gf1pro00.dialogue: ask who the Great Ones are
gf1pro00.speaker: Protagonist

gf1pro01.dialogue: say you are the Great Ones
gf1pro01.speaker: Protagonist

gf1pro02.dialogue: say you are not the Great Ones
gf1pro02.speaker: Protagonist

gf1pro04.dialogue: ask if the Tusk-Lord obeys the Cult
gf1pro04.speaker: Protagonist

tl1tl103.speaker: tusklord
tl1tl103.desc: spoken, awed; 'I ask you, what is greater than the Great Ones?'

tl1dma00.dialogue: The Stone Mouth you carry translates the gargoyle's words.
tl1dma00.speaker: DM

tl1tl105.dialogue: Ah, you are the Great Ones! All the city talks of you. So many creatures you have killed!
tl1tl105.speaker: tusklord

tl1tl106.dialogue: You have made yourselves strong on suffering. I admire that greatly!
tl1tl106.speaker: tusklord

tl1tl107.dialogue: And when I make YOU suffer - think how strong I will be.
tl1tl107.speaker: tusklord

tl1dma01.dialogue: Again, the Stone Mouth you carry translates the gargoyle's words.
tl1dma01.speaker: DM

tl1tl109.dialogue: Yes, they are weaklings, you have done well. Let us feast on their pain!
tl1tl109.speaker: tusklord

gn1gng02.dialogue: Ah, by the Tooth, you have done what we could not - fed the dust to old Gulrithi, and toppled the Skull!
gn1gng02.speaker: Gloran

gn1gu200.dialogue: The foul shades hurt you, I see. The skull totem has tortured us, but what healing we can do, we will.
gn1gu200.speaker: Ethe

gn1gu201.dialogue: Now we must go. For our Shrine sits empty, and we fear the Silver Fire has gone out. Or, worse yet, the Cult of the Dragon has found it.
gn1gu201.speaker: Ethe

gn1gng08.dialogue: Ah! Spit when you say that name! He was a foul crawler, and reeked of hatred.
gn1gng08.speaker: Gloran

gn1gu202.dialogue: For the light of our Shrine, most of all.
gn1gu202.speaker: Ethe

gn1gng09.dialogue: And that led him ever deeper into blackness, and to raise shibboleths to gods we will not name. Gods that feast on pain.
gn1gng09.speaker: Gloran

gn1gu203.dialogue: The Silver Fire is a sisterhood of those who revere Mystra, the Lady of Spells.
gn1gu203.speaker: Ethe

gn1gng12.dialogue: Long ago the high mage Sammaster betrayed Mystra, and used her magic to found the Cult of the Dragon.
gn1gng12.speaker: Gloran

gn1gu204.dialogue: And so the incantrix Yhelfanna founded our Sisterhood, dedicated to undoing the evil Sammaster had done.
gn1gu204.speaker: Ethe

gn1gng14.dialogue: Oh, this is a relief to us! Our Shrine is not abandoned!
gn1gng14.speaker: Gloran

gn1gu205.dialogue: The women you describe must be Sisters of the Silver Fire. Fieryat Ildacer, one of the Seven, told us that a band of Sisters was coming here.
gn1gu205.speaker: Ethe

gn1gng15.dialogue: And small wonder. Ethe and I fear the Cult grows strong here in Myth Drannor.
gn1gng15.speaker: Gloran

gn1gng18.dialogue: Now we must get back to our Shrine.
gn1gng18.speaker: Gloran

gn1gu206.dialogue: Yes, and help our Sisters. Walk with Mystra, until we meet again!
gn1gu206.speaker: Ethe

gn1gng19.dialogue: Now we must get back to our Shrine.
gn1gng19.speaker: Gloran

gn1gu207.dialogue: Walk with Mystra, until we meet again!
gn1gu207.speaker: Ethe

gn1gng21.dialogue: I cannot tell you exactly - because I am not sure where we are. But...
gn1gng21.speaker: Gloran

gn1gng22.dialogue: I believe you go up stairs to get there. And then off to the east, then south, then west.
gn1gng22.speaker: Gloran

gn1gng23.dialogue: The Shrine is hidden from our enemies - but you should find it easily, for clearly the hand of Mystra is upon you.
gn1gng23.speaker: Gloran

gn1gu208.dialogue: The air wafted in to us the sweetest of odors - the scent of another of our kind.
gn1gu208.speaker: Ethe

gn1gng26.dialogue: And so we foolishly left the protection of our Shrine.
gn1gng26.speaker: Gloran

gn1gu209.dialogue: But the scent was false - and led us straight into Gulrithi's trap of pain.
gn1gu209.speaker: Ethe

gn1gng27.dialogue: But how ungrateful we are!  Please accept our thanks for freeing us. The days have been a blur of pain...
gn1gng27.speaker: Gloran

gn1gu210.dialogue: ...and most agonizing of all was the vision of our Shrine unprotected, and our duty a failure. As Gulrithi well knew, when he set his trap for us.
gn1gu210.speaker: Ethe

gn1gng28.dialogue: But you asked how we came to be imprisoned here.
gn1gng28.speaker: Gloran

gn1gng29.dialogue: But you asked about the Silver Fire.
gn1gng29.speaker: Gloran

gn1gng30.dialogue: But you asked where the Shrine of the Silver Fire was.
gn1gng30.speaker: Gloran

gn1gng33.dialogue: May the Lady walk with you. Goodbye.
gn1gng33.speaker: Gloran

gn1pro00.dialogue: Ask them about Gulrithi and Skull
gn1pro00.speaker: Protagonist

gn1pro01.dialogue: Ask them how they got here
gn1pro01.speaker: Protagonist

gn1pro02.dialogue: Ask them where the Shrine is
gn1pro02.speaker: Protagonist

gn1pro03.dialogue: Ask them what the Silver Fire is
gn1pro03.speaker: Protagonist

gn1pro04.dialogue: Tell them about the sisters you met
gn1pro04.speaker: Protagonist

gx2gng02.dialogue: Look, Ethe, our saviors have returned!
gx2gng02.speaker: Gloran

gx2gu200.dialogue: They are hurt! Let us try to heal them.
gx2gu200.speaker: Ethe

gx2gu201.dialogue: And they are unhurt, thank the Lady. We'll save our healing arts for another time.
gx2gu201.speaker: Ethe

gx2gu202.dialogue: And they are unhurt, thank the Lady. Or almost so!
gx2gu202.speaker: Ethe

gx2gng06.dialogue: Their wounds are slight, but let us heal them.
gx2gng06.speaker: Gloran
gx2gng06.desc: spoken, glad to be of service

gx2gu203.dialogue: ...but we will try to heal them.
gx2gu203.speaker: Ethe

gx2gu204.dialogue: Ah - the heroes have come back! Do they need our healing, do you think?
gx2gu204.speaker: Ethe

gx2gng09.dialogue: No! The Hand of the Goddess has preserved them.
gx2gng09.speaker: Gloran

gx2gu205.dialogue: Welcome, travelers, and rest here as long as you like... the Silver Fire will protect you.
gx2gu205.speaker: Ethe

gx2gng10.dialogue: They are not badly hurt.. but let us show them the strength of the Silver Fire.
gx2gng10.speaker: Gloran

gx2gng11.dialogue: Yes! Let us show them the strength of the Silver Fire.
gx2gng11.speaker: Gloran

gx2gng12.dialogue: Welcome back, travelers, to the sanctuary of the Silver Fire.
gx2gng12.speaker: Gloran

gx2gu206.dialogue: Rest here as long as you like.
gx2gu206.speaker: Ethe

gx2gng13.dialogue: Come, Ethe, it is time to summon the healing Fire.
gx2gng13.speaker: Gloran

gx4gng02.dialogue: Ah Ethe, it is them!  The heroes of Myth Drannor!
gx4gng02.speaker: Gloran

gx4gn200.dialogue: See how the flame brightens for them! Welcome heroes! The tales of your deeds precede you!
gx4gn200.speaker: Ethe

gx4gng03.dialogue: Look Ethe, our heroes have returned!
gx4gng03.speaker: Gloran

gx4gn201.dialogue: It is they who slew the dracolich, and crushed the haughty Kya Mordrayn!
gx4gn201.speaker: Ethe

gx4gng04.dialogue: Let us heal those hurts, heroes!  Our shrine is honored by your valor.
gx4gng04.speaker: Gloran
gx4gng04.desc: spoken, administering a blessing, then a goodbye

gx4gng05.dialogue: The Mythal hums in tune again, heroes, thanks to you!
gx4gng05.speaker: Gloran

gx4gn202.dialogue: ...and Mystra rejoices in its song.  Rest here a while and let her blessings flow over you.
gx4gn202.speaker: Ethe

hcyhac02.speaker: Hachaam
hcyhac02.desc: spoken, ghostly wail, 'Faervian', eerie, can't tell what it wants

hcyhac04.dialogue: Faervian. My Baneblade. You have freed it. You can wield it. I am jealous of you.
hcyhac04.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac05.dialogue: You hold Faervian. You may swing it, and cleave your enemies with it...
hcyhac05.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac06.dialogue: ...but the Baneblade will never sing as it did when I flashed it before the Armies of Darkness.
hcyhac06.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac07.dialogue: You may hold it, but it will always be my blade.
hcyhac07.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac08.dialogue: I am... I was... Hachaam Selorn, Arms-Captain of the armies of Myth Drannor.
hcyhac08.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac09.dialogue: But I suppose that means nothing to you now.
hcyhac09.speaker: Hachaam

hcydma00.dialogue: You hold out the sword to the ghost, but it cannot grasp it.
hcydma00.speaker: DM

hcyhac12.dialogue: I will go. But I make a deal with you...
hcyhac12.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac15.dialogue: You will regret that... You must atone... the Rivener...
hcyhac15.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac16.dialogue: Bring Faervian to my tomb... the tomb of Hachaam Selorn... little good my Baneblade will do you now.
hcyhac16.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac17.dialogue: My tomb... bring Faervian to my tomb, the tomb of Hachaam Selorn. I will tell you... of the Rivener... the baneblade Morvian.
hcyhac17.speaker: Hachaam

hcyhac18.dialogue: My tomb... bring Faervian to my tomb. I will tell you... of the Rivener... the baneblade Morvian.
hcyhac18.speaker: Hachaam

hcypro00.dialogue: Ask the ghost who it is
hcypro00.speaker: Protagonist

hcypro02.dialogue: Give the sword to the ghost
hcypro02.speaker: Protagonist

hcypro03.dialogue: Tell the ghost the sword is yours
hcypro03.speaker: Protagonist

hcypro04.dialogue: Tell the ghost to go away
hcypro04.speaker: Protagonist

hcxhac04.dialogue: I thank you for Faervian. It brings me peace to have it by my side once again.
hcxhac04.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac05.dialogue: But hush! In the little time I have left, I must tell you about the Baneblade Morvian.
hcxhac05.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac06.dialogue: It is a greater blade than Faervian, or so many say. For years after the fall of Myth Drannor, the gold dragons kept it...
hcxhac06.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac07.dialogue: ...but it was taken by a fell beast, the Demon Rivener. They could not slay the thing, so they sealed it behind the Glyph of Moon, a majuscule first writ by Corellon Larethian himself.
hcxhac07.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac08.dialogue: But time has weakened the Rivener, or so I believe. And lo! I give you the power to undo the Glyph. Hear now the Rivening Word!
hcxhac08.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac09.dialogue: The Demon Rivener. A fell beast, who hates all light and love, took a treasure from the gold dragons who had protected it for many years.
hcxhac09.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac10.dialogue: They chased the Rivener here, but could not defeat it. And so they sealed it deep underneath the Castle, behind the Glyph of Moon, a majuscule first writ by Corellon Larethian himself.
hcxhac10.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac11.dialogue: The treasure the fiend took? Morvian, which some say is the most powerful of the Baneblades. Ah, it is a thing of beauty, to be sure!
hcxhac11.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac12.dialogue: And it is time that someone undid the Glyph, and confronted the Rivener, and took Morvian to hand once again. So behold! I teach you the Rivening Word!
hcxhac12.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac15.dialogue: Ah you fools... beware the Rivener...
hcxhac15.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac16.dialogue: Behold, I curse you now with the Rivening Word.
hcxhac16.speaker: Hachaam

hcxdma01.dialogue: The ghost opens his mouth, and Ffrakun, a Word of Power, leaps forth.
hcxdma01.speaker: dm

hcxhac18.dialogue: May it serve you as you deserve.
hcxhac18.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac19.dialogue: Use it with care, when you find the circle surrounded by 4 blades, the Glyph of Moon.
hcxhac19.speaker: Hachaam

hcxhac24.dialogue: Before you go, I will teach you a Word of Power, the Rivening Word.
hcxhac24.speaker: Hachaam

hcxpro00.dialogue: Tell the ghost you returned his sword
hcxpro00.speaker: Protagonist

hcxpro01.dialogue: Ask the ghost about the Rivener
hcxpro01.speaker: Protagonist
