ttwinf03.dialogue: This signpost, Playing the Game, can teach you about elements of the interface, or you can ask about things you want to learn how to do.
ttwinf03.speaker: infowell

ttwinf05.dialogue: The round button in the lower left corner breaks away from the game action to mundane bookkeeping functions.
ttwinf05.speaker: infowell

ttwinf06.dialogue: Click on the Game Options button to bring up a menu, from which you can load or save games, quit the game, and change the game settings.
ttwinf06.speaker: infowell

ttwinf07.dialogue: When you are done talking to me, try saving your game. Then, whenever you want to ask me a question, all you have to do is load that saved game.
ttwinf07.speaker: infowell

ttwinf08.dialogue: In the box at the lower left corner of the screen, you'll find a book, a sun, and a map icon. These are the Quest Log, Time of Day, and Map functions, respectively.
ttwinf08.speaker: infowell

ttwinf09.dialogue: Click on the Quest Log book to remind yourself about quests you've heard of, but haven't yet fulfilled.
ttwinf09.speaker: infowell

ttwinf10.dialogue: Check the Sun display for time of day. As night falls, a full sun will wane to dark. Be more careful then, because some creatures only come out at night.
ttwinf10.speaker: infowell

ttwinf11.dialogue: Click on the map to see an overhead view of the area you are exploring. You can drag flags from the right to label areas of the map to remind you where certain things are.
ttwinf11.speaker: infowell

ttwinf12.dialogue: In the box at the lower right corner of the screen, you'll find some colored bars, one for each character in the party.
ttwinf12.speaker: infowell

ttwinf13.dialogue: Clicking on a bar selects a character, just as if you had clicked on the character directly. You'll see the highlight box jump to the character you've selected.
ttwinf13.speaker: infowell

ttwinf14.dialogue: The height of the bar indicates the health of the character. When you are in combat, keep your eye on those bars, so you can heal wounded characters or pull them out of danger.
ttwinf14.speaker: infowell

ttwinf15.dialogue: The colored rings underneath a character match that person's colored bar, both in appearance and in function.
ttwinf15.speaker: infowell

ttwinf16.dialogue: Three rings means the character is healthy; with two, they're damaged; if there is only one, the character is hurting.
ttwinf16.speaker: infowell

ttwinf17.dialogue: Red rings appear under enemies, and follow the same system: three means the monster is healthy, two damaged, and one in bad shape.  Watching the red rings under opponents can help guide your combat strategy.
ttwinf17.speaker: infowell

ttwinf18.dialogue: One more thing: the small triangle points to your current party leader. If you want to change leaders, click-drag the triangle to point at a new character.
ttwinf18.speaker: infowell

ttwinf19.dialogue: In the box at the lower right corner of the screen, you'll find two square buttons, one on top of the other. The top one is the Party Formation button; the bottom is the Rest button.
ttwinf19.speaker: infowell

ttwinf20.dialogue: To set your party's marching formation, first arrange the characters the way you'd like them. Then click the Party Formation button.
ttwinf20.speaker: infowell

ttwinf21.dialogue: Tip: it's generally a good idea to have your party leader at the front of your formation.
ttwinf21.speaker: infowell

ttwinf22.dialogue: Click the bottom button when you want your party to rest and relearn their spells. You can learn more about resting elsewhere in the tutorial.
ttwinf22.speaker: infowell

ttwinf23.dialogue: The round button in the lower right corner of the screen is the Group/Ungroup button. To group all your characters together, and move them in formation, click the button so that it displays three little figures.
ttwinf23.speaker: infowell

ttwinf24.dialogue: If you click on a character or its colored bar, this button will change to a single large figure. You can now move that character independently of the others, to scout for traps or secret doors, smash objects, and so on.
ttwinf24.speaker: infowell

ttwinf25.dialogue: To move again as a group, click on the Group/Ungroup button so that it again displays three little figures. But heed this: you can't group your characters when you are in combat.
ttwinf25.speaker: infowell

ttwinf26.dialogue: When you move your characters as a group, everyone follows the 'party leader.' You select your leader using the small triangle below the colored bars in the box in the lower right corner of the screen.
ttwinf26.speaker: infowell

ttwinf27.dialogue: The leader not only heads up the party, but speaks for the party to characters you meet, and interacts with objects when the party is acting as a group.
ttwinf27.speaker: infowell

ttwinf28.dialogue: To change the party leader, click on the triangle and, while holding down the mouse button, slide the triangle underneath another colored bar.
ttwinf28.speaker: infowell

ttwinf29.dialogue: Sometimes you may find that one of the icon boxes covers up a part of the screen you would like to see.
ttwinf29.speaker: infowell

ttwinf30.dialogue: To make the icon box pop down out of the way, click on the small diamond at the bottom center of the icon box. To bring it back up, click on the small diamond at the top center, the only part still showing.
ttwinf30.speaker: infowell

ttwdma00.dialogue: Goodbye. To review this information, come back here and click on this signpost.
ttwdma00.speaker: DM

kwxDMYF.dialogue: With some effort your elf can trace the path, and spots the place where it emerges at the top, and disappears into the darkness under the trees of the Glim-Garden.

kwsDMYA.dialogue: Along the arch is written, in the languages of elves, dwarves, humans and wizards, 'Speculum - Great Hall of Wizards.'
kwsDMYA.speaker: DM

kwsDMYB.dialogue: Through the arch, you see the Spire of Mythanthor, where you first came up from the Dungeons. And, rising behind it, you see the Speculum, which once was the seat of power for Myth Drannor's magical elite.
kwsDMYB.speaker: DM

kwnDMYA.dialogue: To the north, a narrow path switchbacks its way up a steep cliff.
kwnDMYA.speaker: DM

kwnDMYB.dialogue: Up at the top, you see the trees and elevated walkways of the Windrider Glade.
kwnDMYB.speaker: DM

kwrDMYA.dialogue: Faint runes run across the arch, announcing the entrance to the 'Noble House of Omberdawn.'
kwrDMYA.speaker: DM

kwrDMYB.dialogue: But the runes no longer tell the truth. Instead, beyond the archway, you see the expanse of soggy ground known as Sullymarsh.
kwrDMYB.speaker: DM

kwtDMYA.dialogue: The stone path continues to the west. At its end, you can make out one of Myth Drannor's great city squares, the Nightingale Court.
kwtDMYA.speaker: DM

kwtDMYB.dialogue: The proud buildings and public spaces are still elegant, even in ruin.
kwtDMYB.speaker: DM

kwtDMYC.dialogue: The stone path continues to the west. At its end, even in the gloom of night, you can make out the silhouettes of buildings.
kwtDMYC.speaker: DM

kwtDMYD.dialogue: This is the Nightingale Court, one of Myth Drannor's great city squares. The proud buildings and public spaces are still elegant, even in ruin.

wh1whi02.dialogue: O Citizen of Myth Drannor, what thing do you seek?
wh1whi02.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi03.dialogue: Treasures pass from hand to hand, from hoard to hoard, yet I hear where they go. Ask me.
wh1whi03.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi04.dialogue: O Citizen of Myth Drannor, what manner of thing do you seek?
wh1whi04.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi05.dialogue: O Citizen, now what treasure do you seek? Ask - but hurry! For I have not much time.
wh1whi05.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi06.dialogue: O Citizen, I have no more stories to tell. A hush has fallen over the City, and words fail me.
wh1whi06.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi07.dialogue: I am the Ear of the City. I listen and remember.
wh1whi07.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi08.dialogue: In happier days I listened for glad tidings, and repeated them so all would be happy. I helped citizens find things that were lost...
wh1whi08.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi09.dialogue: ...now I listen to the wails of the dying, and repeat the evil mutterings of monsters clutching their treasures down in the dark.
wh1whi09.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi11.dialogue: You think not? Yet all the city talks about you - the stones themselves whisper your names as you pass.
wh1whi11.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi12.dialogue: You are the best citizens the city could hope for in these dark days, and all the city's treasures are yours, if you wish them.
wh1whi12.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi13.dialogue: I hear about powerful things of magic - such as rings, wands and scrolls. I hear about arms and armor, and other weapons of war. And I hear about jewels, books and other treasures.
wh1whi13.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi14.dialogue: But be quick! For I cannot talk for long.
wh1whi14.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi18.dialogue: I am sorry. The Whispering Wind speaks no more of rings or necklaces.
wh1whi18.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi19.dialogue: I heard, long ago, a dwarf woman speak of an amulet - Onglore's Amulet of War. She said...
wh1whi19.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi20.dialogue: 'Here ya go, my husband. It was yours in life, so shall it be yours in death.' And the Amulet hummed as she laid it down.
wh1whi20.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi21.dialogue: The voice wafted up to me from the Main Halls of the Dungeons.
wh1whi21.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi23.dialogue: Not so long ago a voice spoke over a locket - it was Tyr's Locket of Justice. The voice said...
wh1whi23.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi24.dialogue: 'You will summon the Nightmare Gate here. This scroll bears the Word of Constriction. When the time comes, it will dispel the Gate. In the meantime, use this.' And the Locket clinked as the mage put it on.
wh1whi24.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi25.dialogue: That little clinking sound skittered down the Stone Halls of the Dungeons, and crawled into my ear.
wh1whi25.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi26.dialogue: Again and again over the centuries, I hear voices curse at Aasirak's Ebony Ring Of Power.
wh1whi26.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi27.dialogue: 'Aaaagh! I cannot lift it!' they all say, and with sorrow they leave it behind.
wh1whi27.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi28.dialogue: Some drow were the last to say it, before their souls went dark, deep in the Catacombs.
wh1whi28.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi30.dialogue: Why, there are drow talking about the Eye Of The Witch, right this moment!
wh1whi30.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi31.dialogue: One is saying, 'For priest or mage, it is a boon. Let us return immediately with this charm! I sense a reward!'
wh1whi31.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi32.dialogue: And now another says, 'The glory of Freth is reward enough. Come, let us go.'
wh1whi32.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi33.dialogue: And now the whisper of drow boots on stone, as soft as a caress, in the deepest chambers of the Catacombs.
wh1whi33.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi36.dialogue: I recall hearing a dwarf voice boom out above a necklace - the Onyx of the Richest Wort. This was hundreds of years ago.
wh1whi36.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi37.dialogue: 'The city be surrounded,' the voice said. 'Dumathoin aid us, we must hide what we can, destroy what we must, and drink the rest.'
wh1whi37.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi38.dialogue: Then I heard the tink-clink of valuables being hidden away. All has been silent ever since, down in the Brewer's Chambers of the Halls of Light, in the Dungeons.
wh1whi38.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi40.dialogue: I will tell you what I heard several days ago, with the Pendant of Fresh Kills.
wh1whi40.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi41.dialogue: The thunder of battle magic fades away. A woman gasps her dying breath. Clutching the Pendant, she utters these words: 'Bright fire, white fire, Silver Pyre, let this body burn.'
wh1whi41.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi42.dialogue: A roar erupts - mages scream - and she and her Pendant are nothing but ashes whispering through the air.
wh1whi42.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi46.dialogue: This is what I heard many centuries ago, from the wearer of the Ring of Equilibrium.
wh1whi46.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi47.dialogue: He said, 'Watch out, ya clummoxy hamhand! If I hadna been wearing this Ring, ya might have killed me with that.'
wh1whi47.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi48.dialogue: Today, however, the Ring is scorned by its owner, and lies quiet and forgotten in a chest, in the uppermost part of the Catacombs.
wh1whi48.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi51.dialogue: O, I know of a necklace, the wonderful Necklace of Odoacer. Let me listen now...
wh1whi51.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi52.dialogue: Yes, it is underwater. It has been underwater for centuries now. Out of the roaring flames it flew, into the cool silence of deep water...
wh1whi52.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi53.dialogue: Now once again I hear the Watersong of Plinshree. Do you know of her, the naiad of this place? She is the only one who could retrieve this necklace for you, from its watery grave.
wh1whi53.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi56.dialogue: No more of that. You know all you should of the city's objects of magic.
wh1whi56.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi61.dialogue: Ah, there is a wand, Terrilan's Crimson Wand - an accusing voice follows this wand wherever it goes.
wh1whi61.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi62.dialogue: 'Terrilan, you killed your brother,' the voice whispers. 'Terrilan Grandirons, where is your brother Herunga?' Because of the voice, the nagas who possess it do not use the wand.
wh1whi62.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi63.dialogue: These sounds floated up to me from the upper reaches of the Catacombs.
wh1whi63.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi65.dialogue: Wait, I hear the crinkle of paper. Someone has taken a scroll out of a leather pouch...
wh1whi65.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi66.dialogue: Now a harsh voice says, 'Look at this. It's a Word of Power!'
wh1whi66.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi67.dialogue: And now another voice says - but no! It screams! A death cry... clicking mandibles... a magic Gate, closing...
wh1whi67.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi68.dialogue: ...and now the sounds of beasts feasting, far away and down deep, below the Dungeons.
wh1whi68.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi70.dialogue: So wands interest you? I heard someone speak in the presence of the Sceptre Of Leogans.
wh1whi70.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi71.dialogue: He said, 'Of course you are right, Mistress. Someone gives them aid. But who?' And then, 'Fanraet is very capable. The witches must have used some trick.'
wh1whi71.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi72.dialogue: And then finally he said, 'Of course, Mistress. Yes. At once.' His voice, stammering with fear, echoed up from the middle depths of the Catacombs.
wh1whi72.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi75.dialogue: I can tell you what I heard about the Scroll of Memory, writ by Shyael Ildacer, a High Court Mage, just before the fall of Myth Drannor.
wh1whi75.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi76.dialogue: When the Army of Darkness invaded the city, the scroll was lost beneath some rubble. But a year ago dark nagas found it, and used its Remembering Word to bring back forgotten magics.
wh1whi76.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi77.dialogue: They might have learned some ancient spells of incalculable power! But a fortnight ago Pelendralaar came and killed them all, and ruined their lair, and utterly destroyed the Scroll of Memory.
wh1whi77.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi79.dialogue: I know of a scroll - Kiaransalee's Scroll of Claim - let me listen to what is going on around this scroll.
wh1whi79.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi80.dialogue: A man is speaking. He has a dead voice! He is berating someone for their failure. They have not found a book he seeks... He shakes the scroll at them!
wh1whi80.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi81.dialogue: I hear the quick harsh breath of lizardfolk! They hiss. Now they go away, leaving the man in silence... This I hear clearly, even though it is happening far off to the west.
wh1whi81.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi85.dialogue: Hmmm... here is a stick, Roderick's Walkingstick! Let me open my ears to it...
wh1whi85.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi86.dialogue: No, no, all is quiet where it lies. Except - a rustling noise, such as rats might make, or some other creature more stealthy.
wh1whi86.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi87.dialogue: This staff lies barely underground, some distance to the west.
wh1whi87.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi91.dialogue: No, no, the winds blow ill. We must talk no more about things of war.
wh1whi91.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi92.dialogue: Oh, there is a shield, and terrible sounds surround this shield!
wh1whi92.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi93.dialogue: I hear the slavering howls of the undead, and the snap-tattoo of cruel traps, and the insane shrieking of victims caught in barbs or liquid fire.
wh1whi93.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi94.dialogue: The shield is Gnome's Shield of Invulnerability, and its sounds echoed up from behind a secret door in the Main Halls of the Dungeons.
wh1whi94.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi96.dialogue: Silence, silence surrounds the Sword of Marshbane, as it has for years uncounted.
wh1whi96.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi97.dialogue: Only the faintest rustling in the old armory, the sound of a haunt endlessly pacing.
wh1whi97.speaker: Whisper

wh1whi98.dialogue: These sounds drift on the winds to me, from the dark place that once was called the Halls of Light.
wh1whi98.speaker: Whisper

wh1whia0.dialogue: I heard someone carrying magical mail armor - this was many years ago. And they laid it gently into a chest, and whispered a benison, and closed the lid.
wh1whia0.speaker: Whisper

wh1whia1.dialogue: Oh! That armor laughed as they laid it down! It sounded like water falling! It must be excellently made.
wh1whia1.speaker: Whisper

wh1whia2.dialogue: I heard this sound very clearly. It was near at hand, and only a spear's length or two underground.
wh1whia2.speaker: Whisper

wh1whia4.dialogue: I remember hearing about a staff - the famous Guulstav Of M'raelhorrid.
wh1whia4.speaker: Whisper

wh1whia5.dialogue: It was a woman's voice, lovely and low. She said, 'And I have reserved the best for my loyal Mage Captain. Here - this is reward for your excellent work regarding our ally, the Baelnorn.
wh1whia5.speaker: Whisper

wh1whia6.dialogue: Her voice echoed up from the deepest chambers of the Catacombs under the Castle.
wh1whia6.speaker: Whisper

wh1whib0.dialogue: I have heard a sound related to Quimbee's Armor Of Many Pockets.
wh1whib0.speaker: Whisper

wh1whib1.dialogue: A drow woman is speaking - her voice is thrilling. 'Box it up,' she says in the drow tongue. 'The Matron Mother will be most pleased.'
wh1whib1.speaker: Whisper

wh1whib2.dialogue: Her voice rang along the hard stones and gloomy halls of the Catacombs.
wh1whib2.speaker: Whisper

wh1whib4.dialogue: Here is a fearsome weapon - which some call the Deathspike. I hear sounds around it...
wh1whib4.speaker: Whisper

wh1whib5.dialogue: ...the tramp of lizardy feet, and grumbling voices. 'I do not care what we promised,' the leader says. 'This is strong magic - it must go to Malgi Hi.' And now the feet tramp on, up stairs of stone and into the light.
wh1whib5.speaker: Whisper

wh1whib6.dialogue: This sound wafted over to me from the ruins to the north.
wh1whib6.speaker: Whisper

wh1whib8.dialogue: Here is something I heard, said in the presence of the Muttering Axe.
wh1whib8.speaker: Whisper

wh1whib9.dialogue: 'My Mistress bids you receive this as a token of her esteem. She hopes it aids you as you rise in stature among the Ormyrrs.'
wh1whib9.speaker: Whisper

wh1whic0.dialogue: This voice floated up from the Marshes to the south, about a fortnight ago.
wh1whic0.speaker: Whisper

wh1whic2.dialogue: Now I have heard the song of Prince Antonae's Stormbow - which makes arrows sing with delight!
wh1whic2.speaker: Whisper

wh1whic3.dialogue: But that was in the past, when Lord Derrose wielded it in Myth Drannor's final days, and when Jada Moonglamaer took it up, after Derrose fell.
wh1whic3.speaker: Whisper

wh1whic4.dialogue: Now the bow listens sadly as mandibles clack and bones split, down in an arraccat's lair deep in the Catacombs.
wh1whic4.speaker: Whisper

wh1whic6.dialogue: I know the Wraithmael Of Drenofiend has been laid to rest.
wh1whic6.speaker: Whisper

wh1whic7.dialogue: Drenofiend was a half-ogre, bane of elves... He died, praise Corellan, in the final assault on the city, and his ancient armor tumbled into deep places and was lost.
wh1whic7.speaker: Whisper

wh1whic8.dialogue: But naught that is buried is buried for ever. The drow have brought the Wraithmael back up from the deeps, and hold it in a secret chamber in the center of their stronghold.
wh1whic8.speaker: Whisper

wh1whic9.dialogue: 'Wait here,' they whisper to it in their language. 'One is coming, worthy of you. Be patient.'
wh1whic9.speaker: Whisper

wh1whid0.dialogue: I remember sounds I heard, extraordinary sounds, associated with the axe called Wroth's Executioner.
wh1whid0.speaker: Whisper

wh1whid1.dialogue: Wroth, who styled himself Wroth the Indestructible, was killed at last by the dwarf-captain Artoth Freyhammer, with one mighty blow that shattered his knee. Wroth died from the pain...
wh1whid1.speaker: Whisper

wh1whid2.dialogue: ...and the wail of his passing was mortifying to behold! Yet Artoth withstood it, and claimed the Executioner for his own...
wh1whid2.speaker: Whisper

wh1whid3.dialogue: ...and was buried with it, down in the Royal Tombs reserved for dwarves, deep in the silent Catacombs.
wh1whid3.speaker: Whisper

wh1whid6.dialogue: I have said all I should about such things. Do not ask me for more.
wh1whid6.speaker: Whisper

wh1whid7.dialogue: I heard the sound of a pen writing in a book. Every day I heard it - oh, this was many many years ago.
wh1whid7.speaker: Whisper

wh1whid8.dialogue: And then the writer spoke. She said, 'It is a terrible risk, to strike the spark of life among the dead! But I must try it - or the City will be lost!' And she never wrote in that book again.
wh1whid8.speaker: Whisper

wh1whid9.dialogue: That was deep, deep down in the Catacombs, but yet I heard it distinctly.
wh1whid9.speaker: Whisper

wh1whie1.dialogue: I heard someone talk about a pair of boots...
wh1whie1.speaker: Whisper

wh1whie2.dialogue: He was quite upset. 'Ozama, you have tricked me!' he shrieked. 'Nothing for the neck - nothing! Your powerful magic is on your feet! What good is that to me? Snakeskin - pah!'
wh1whie2.speaker: Whisper

wh1whie3.dialogue: And he threw the boots out the door, into some garbage, and the sound they made sailed out of the Dungeon's Main Halls and into my ears.
wh1whie3.speaker: Whisper

wh1whie5.dialogue: Well, very recently I heard a man running and dodging.
wh1whie5.speaker: Whisper

wh1whie6.dialogue: He was cursing under his breath. He said, 'Sammaster, aid me!' And all the while I could hear zombies moaning and the foul jeering of orcs.
wh1whie6.speaker: Whisper

wh1whie7.dialogue: And then at last he screamed and died, and the boots he was wearing stayed with his body, far in the Main Halls of the Dungeons.
wh1whie7.speaker: Whisper

wh1whie9.dialogue: Maybe you are interested in a lamp. I know of one, and can hear the sounds around it...
wh1whie9.speaker: Whisper

wh1whif0.dialogue: ...margoyles jeering at some creature, and baiting it cruelly, as margoyles do.
wh1whif0.speaker: Whisper

wh1whif1.dialogue: 'Come out into the light!' they say. 'Oh, does that bother you? Does this hurt? Does this hurt even more? Oik oik ik ik ik!'
wh1whif1.speaker: Whisper

wh1whif2.dialogue: These sounds, and many more besides, traveled up from the second floor of the Catacombs.
wh1whif2.speaker: Whisper

wh1whif5.dialogue: Here is an unusual thing - the Boots of Beguiling Gait.
wh1whif5.speaker: Whisper

wh1whif6.dialogue: I hear a woman's voice, ghostly and wan. She laments that none but evil creatures come to her tomb. Her boots go unused, and she, like her beloved city, is dishonored and unmourned.
wh1whif6.speaker: Whisper

wh1whif7.dialogue: Her voice drifted up to me from deep down in the Catacombs.
wh1whif7.speaker: Whisper

wh1whif9.dialogue: Near here I sense a very precious thing - one of the Starstones of old.
wh1whif9.speaker: Whisper

wh1whig0.dialogue: I remember long, long ago, I heard a dwarf say, 'Ya must take it out! The enemy is almost here. The Circle must be closed.' And then the sound of beautiful metal wrenched apart.
wh1whig0.speaker: Whisper

wh1whig1.dialogue: That was long ago. Today, the Starstone rests in the House of Gems - in silence, but for a sad and faint heartbeat.
wh1whig1.speaker: Whisper

wh1whig3.dialogue: I heard something spoken over some very handsome boots, the Boots of Stalking.
wh1whig3.speaker: Whisper

wh1whig4.dialogue: A lieutenant of the Cult said it, not very long ago: 'You two! Let them be, they're dead, can't you see that?'
wh1whig4.speaker: Whisper

wh1whig5.dialogue: Take the Captain's body with us, leave the others behind. And you! Fetch me the boots off that Orog assassin. Amazing what that one Orog could do, with those boots on.'
wh1whig5.speaker: Whisper

wh1whig6.dialogue: This voice wafted up to me, out of the middle depths of the Catacombs.
wh1whig6.speaker: Whisper

wh1whig7.dialogue: Hush! I will listen close to those magic gauntlets, the Daemonclaws Of Gr'zak.
wh1whig7.speaker: Whisper

wh1whig8.dialogue: Over its short life, hundreds have died for them. But what is this? All is quiet, where they are.
wh1whig8.speaker: Whisper

wh1whig9.dialogue: No! Wait! I hear the faintest of rustling, like cobwebs in moonbreeze. And this faintest of sounds emanates from the very deepest part of the Catacombs.
wh1whig9.speaker: Whisper

wh1whih1.dialogue: Oh, I will tell you what I heard spoken near the Gauntlets of Moander.
wh1whih1.speaker: Whisper

wh1whih2.dialogue: The man Athan no longer holds them! They were seized by emissaries of the Cult, and passed from hand to hand to Kya Mordrayn herself.
wh1whih2.speaker: Whisper

wh1whih3.dialogue: 'That is well,' she said when she got them. The only way to destroy a Pool of Radiance, and it falls into her hands!
wh1whih3.speaker: Whisper

wh1whih4.dialogue: 'That is well,' she said. Her voice echoed up dark tunnels, all the way from a deep cavern beneath Castle Cormanthor.
wh1whih4.speaker: Whisper

wh1whih5.dialogue: I know of some gauntlets - the Gauntlets of Light Burden.
wh1whih5.speaker: Whisper

wh1whih6.dialogue: I was listening when the elves that bore them were overcome by gargoyles... how the elves screamed before they died! It almost made me stop up my ears.
wh1whih6.speaker: Whisper

wh1whih7.dialogue: But now, let me listen... gargoyles still hold the gauntlets, I hear their cruel sniggering. Now I hear wings - they have taken flight - now they land on some tower, and squabble and curse as they perch there.
wh1whih7.speaker: Whisper

wh1whih8.dialogue: These sounds came from not too far away, north and east of here.
wh1whih8.speaker: Whisper

wh1whii0.dialogue: I will tell you about a curious prize, the Stone Mouth.
wh1whii0.speaker: Whisper

wh1whii1.dialogue: Once it belonged to Odelinde, the serpent - have you met her? She dwells west and north of here, in the Wind Rider's Shrine.
wh1whii1.speaker: Whisper

wh1whii2.dialogue: But I was listening when two thieves pilfered it from her shrine. Drunk on their cleverness, they made their way to the southeast... and came quite close to me...
wh1whii2.speaker: Whisper

wh1whii3.dialogue: But then came such a sound, as if the earth had swallowed them up! And ever since then, the Stone Mouth has lain in quiet darkness.
wh1whii3.speaker: Whisper

wh1whii6.dialogue: But hush now! The beasts cry out - can you hear it? I must go.
wh1whii6.speaker: Whisper

wh1whii7.dialogue: But I am out of time. Goodbye for now.
wh1whii7.speaker: Whisper

wh1whii8.dialogue: But that is all I can tell you now. Come see me again.
wh1whii8.speaker: Whisper

wh1whii9.dialogue: But now I can say no more. Goodbye.
wh1whii9.speaker: Whisper

wh1whij0.dialogue: But that is all I will say, until we meet again.
wh1whij0.speaker: Whisper

wh1whij1.dialogue: But now - the wind falters - the chaos returns. I must go.
wh1whij1.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYB.dialogue: But hush! I hear the Song of Faerun. And the Bard of Kara-Tur is singing about you! Two stanzas! Do you wish to hear them, as you walk away?
wh1whiYB.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYC.dialogue: O Citizen, which part will you hear?
wh1whiYC.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYD.dialogue: Very well... what manner of treasure do you seek?
wh1whiYD.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYJ.dialogue: Very well then! Listen to the Song of Faerun.
wh1whiYJ.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYK.dialogue: Shall I tell you what I heard about the treasures of Myth Drannor?
wh1whiYK.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYL.dialogue: Oh, there is a weapon, a sacred weapon, the Helm Cleaver. Much talk surrounds it!
wh1whiYL.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYM.dialogue: Orogs come and demand it. But human voices say 'No, no, not yet. You have not earned it yet.' And orog voices protest in anger and go away, muttering and scheming.
wh1whiYM.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYN.dialogue: This I have heard in the uppermost halls of the Dungeons.
wh1whiYN.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYP.dialogue: Oh, I hear a woman wailing, she cries out for a token, a parchment, a blazoned shield, a medallion - any proof that her goddess is remembered!
wh1whiYP.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYQ.dialogue: But evil hisses drown out her cries and deepen her sorrows.
wh1whiYQ.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYR.dialogue: This I have heard echoing down the ruined ways here in the Nightingale Court.
wh1whiYR.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYT.dialogue: Now I hear two people at prayer, their voices mumbling together the name of Mystra.
wh1whiYT.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYU.dialogue: He humbly asks the Goddess of Mystery to look with favor on those she has marked to pursue the vital quest.
wh1whiYU.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYV.dialogue: But his companion, Faeril, is not so devout! Her voice is loud and her prayer much like a demand! 'Mystra, you will do this!' she cries! She slaps a medallion down on the table!
wh1whiYV.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYW.dialogue: But his companion, Faeril, is not so devout! Her voice is loud and her prayer much like a demand! 'Mystra, you will do this!' she cries! And the old man raps his staff on the table, to quiet her.
wh1whiYW.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYX.dialogue: But his companion, Faeril, is not so devout! Her voice is loud and her prayer much like a demand! 'Mystra, you will do this!' she cries! She raps a mace upon a table!
wh1whiYX.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiYY.dialogue: But his companion, Faeril, is not so devout! Her voice is loud and her prayer much like a demand! 'Mystra, you will do this!' she cries! She slaps a medallion down on the table, and it rings like a bell!
wh1whiYY.speaker: Whisper

wh1whiY[.dialogue: This I have heard from a sheltered room, up north in Stillwater.
wh1whiY[.speaker: Whisper

wm1DM00.dialogue: The Book taught you the Word of Mystra. It has no other secrets to teach you.
wm1DM00.speaker: DM

wm1DM01.dialogue: The elves' holy book teaches you Alahnmalyr, the Word of Mystra. This Word of Power will speak itself to unseal the glyph of Mystra.
wm1DM01.speaker: DM

wonDM00.dialogue: Kehelben, the Word of Necessity, unseals the Glyph of Safekeeping.
wonDM00.speaker: DM

wondma00.dialogue: You can tell the magic seal in front of this door is both ancient and elvish. But you do not know the Word of Power that will unseal the Glyph.
wondma00.speaker: DM

worDM00.dialogue: The Word of Redemption summons Miroden Silverblade.
worDM00.speaker: DM
worDM00.desc: spoken, this is a big deal & a bit of a surprise

wriDM00.dialogue: The Rivening Word, Frakkun, unseals the Glyph of Moon.
wriDM00.speaker: DM

wridmaYA.dialogue: This sigil of the moon is famous: it represents Corellon Larethian, the protector-god of the elves.
wridmaYA.speaker: DM

jbudma00.dialogue: You sense you would need strong magic to open this seal.
jbudma00.speaker: DM

jbudma01.dialogue: You draw close to the Seal of Mythanthor. You have the Ring of Calling on your finger...
jbudma01.speaker: DM

jbudma02.dialogue: It teaches you Ilycaram, the Calling Word!
jbudma02.speaker: DM

jbudma03.dialogue: You draw close to the Seal of Mythanthor. You slip the Ring of Calling on your finger...
jbudma03.speaker: DM

jbudma04.dialogue: It teaches you Ilycaram, the Calling Word!
jbudma04.speaker: DM

jbudmaYA.dialogue: The Word you speak unseals the ancient portal. You pass through, up to the open air of the City Heights.
jbudmaYA.speaker: DM
